title: 成化十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
應天府鄉試錄序
昔我
太祖高皇帝誕膺
天命奄有萬方以賢才為致治之
本而科目乃得賢之階肆
詔天下三年一賓興賢能用勷
相我
===
國家
列聖相承胥此是重故百有餘年
士之由此出以建勳業揚休
光者不可勝紀昔人所謂豪
傑之士由之而進者蓋於
今日尤盛乃成化十年復當大
比之秋應天府尹臣崇志府丞

比之秋應天府尹〔臣崇志〕府丞
punctuated:
應天府鄉試錄序
昔我太祖高皇帝誕膺天命，奄有萬方，以賢才為致治之本，而科目乃得賢之階，肆詔天下，三年一賓興賢能，用勷相我國家。列聖相承，胥此是重。故百有餘年，士之由此出以建勳業、揚休光者，不可勝紀。昔人所謂「豪傑之士由之而進」者，蓋於今日尤盛。乃成化十年，復當大比之秋，應天府尹臣崇志、府丞
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Yingtian Prefectural Provincial Examination

In the past, our Grand Progenitor, Emperor Gao (Taizu, the Hongwu Emperor), grandly received the Mandate of Heaven and came to possess all regions of the world. Taking worthy talents to be the foundation for achieving good governance, and the civil service examination system to be the stepping stone for obtaining the worthy, he thereupon issued an edict to the empire that every three years the worthy and able should be ceremonially recommended and selected, so as to assist and serve our Dynasty. The successive Sacred Emperors who inherited the throne have all attached great importance to this. Therefore, for more than a hundred years, the scholars who have emerged through this channel to establish meritorious achievements and spread glorious renown are beyond counting. What men of the past meant by saying that "outstanding heroes advance through this system" is indeed especially flourishing today. Now, in the tenth year of the Chenghua reign (1474), it was once again the autumn of the triennial examination. Your servant [Bi] Chongzhi 畢崇志, Prefect of Yingtian Prefecture, and the Vice Prefect, …

title: 成化十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
臣昂先期奏請考試官
上以命諭德臣一夔修撰臣璟臣等
既受
命夙夜兼程而往至則同考試
官教授臣英學正臣淵教諭
臣瑄臣惟恭臣敏臣必顯臣宗禮臣
宗本監試官監察御史臣謙臣
===
祐與凡内外諸執事皆極一
時所聘選而提調則臣崇志焉
既鎖院臣等曁同考官誓之
而后從事盖欲各公厥心以
共厥事期必得豪傑之士以
弼成
昌明之治用不負

時所聘選而提調則臣崇志焉
既鎖院臣等暨同考官誓之
而后從事蓋欲各公厥心以
共厥事期必得豪傑之士以
𤅢成

punctuated: 臣昂先期奏請考試官，上以命諭德臣一夔、修撰臣璟。臣等既受命，夙夜兼程而往。至則同考試官教授臣英、學正臣淵、教諭臣瑄、臣惟恭、臣敏、臣必顯、臣宗禮、臣宗本，監試官監察御史臣謙、臣祐，與凡内外諸執事，皆極一時所聘選，而提調則臣崇志焉。既鎖院，臣等曁同考官誓之而后從事，盖欲各公厥心，以共厥事，期必得豪傑之士，以弼成昌明之治，用不負
translation_en: … your servant Ang submitted a memorial in advance requesting Examiners. His Majesty thereupon appointed Admonisher your servant Yikui and Senior Compiler your servant Jing. Once we, your servants, had received the command, we traveled day and night at double speed. Upon our arrival, the Associate Examiners—Prefectural Instructor your servant Ying, Subprefectural Instructor your servant Yuan, and County Instructors your servants Xuan, Weigong, Min, Bixian, Zongli, and Zongben—along with the Monitoring Officials, Investigating Censors your servants Qian and You, as well as all the various functionaries of the inner and outer wards, were all the finest among those invited and selected at the time; while the Proctor was your servant Chongzhi. Once the examination compound was locked, we, your servants, together with the Associate Examiners, took an oath before commencing our duties. For we desired that each of us should make his mind impartial in order to carry out this shared task with reverence, hoping surely to obtain men of outstanding talent to assist in bringing about a flourishing and enlightened reign, thereby not failing to live up to …

title: 成化十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
朝廷之所簡命時太學洎畿內
士之就試者二千三百有奇
比撤棘得中式者百三十有
五人遵
定制也爰次第其氏名并采其
文之尤醇粹者鋟梓為錄進
之
===
天府傳之海內士之登名于是
者亦榮矣哉行將捷春闈奉
廷對鴻漸之羽翱翔于天矣可
不以豪傑自期待乎夫豪傑
之士必以天下為心身天下
之責者也堯舜吾
君唐虞吾民耻一夫之不獲正巳
alt_text:
朝廷之所簡命時太學洎畿內
士之就試者二千三百有竒
比撤棘得中式者百三十有
五人遵
定制也爰次第其氏名并采其
文之尤醇粹者鋟梓為録進
之
===
天府傳之海內士之登名于是
者亦榮矣哉行將捷春闈奉
廷對鴻漸之羽翺翔于天矣可
不以豪傑自期待乎夫豪傑
之士必以天下為心身天下
之責者也堯舜吾
君唐虞吾民恥一夫之不獲正已
punctuated: 朝廷之所簡命。時太學洎畿內士之就試者，二千三百有奇。比撤棘，得中式者百三十有五人，遵定制也。爰次第其氏名，并采其文之尤醇粹者，鋟梓為錄，進之天府，傳之海內。士之登名于是者，亦榮矣哉！行將捷春闈，奉廷對，鴻漸之羽，翱翔于天矣，可不以豪傑自期待乎？夫豪傑之士，必以天下為心，身天下之責者也。堯舜吾君，唐虞吾民，耻一夫之不獲，正巳
translation_en: … the selective appointment of the Imperial Court. At the time, scholars from the National University and from within the Capital Area who sat for the examination numbered over two thousand three hundred. When the examination compound was opened, one hundred and thirty-five men had passed the required standard, in compliance with the established quota. Thereupon we arranged their names in order and selected the purest and most refined of their essays to be carved on woodblocks as a record, to be presented to the imperial archives and circulated throughout the empire. How glorious indeed it is for the scholars whose names are inscribed herein! Before long, they will triumph in the spring Metropolitan Examination and attend the Palace Examination; like the wild goose advancing by degrees, their wings will soar across the heavens. How could they not hold themselves to the expectation of being outstanding heroes? Now, a scholar of heroic stature necessarily takes the empire as his mind and bears upon himself the responsibility for the empire. Seeking to make our sovereign like Yao and Shun, and our people like those of Tang and Yu, feeling shame if even a single man fails to find his place, rectifying oneself…

title: 成化十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
而物正如古所謂大人者其
上也贊襄謀謨黼黻政令
朝廷倚為重輕天下繫其安危
如古所謂社稷臣者其次也
其或當一面守一郡典一邑
勤勞宣於方岳愷悌洽于閭
里如古所謂王之藩屏民之
===
父母者又其次也隨所任使
要皆殫厥心力有益於
國家有益於生民而后可若乃
儋爵食祿而徒庸庸碌碌無
所為於時與夫衎衎焉營營
焉以圖其私便是皆不恤瘝
曠之誚負乘之譏為庸俗所

朝廷倚為重輕天下繫其安危

其或當一面守一郡典一邑
勤勞宣於方岳愷悌洽于閭
里如古所謂王之藩屏民之
===
父母者又其次也隨所任使
要皆殫厥心力有益於
國家有益於生民而后可若乃
僭爵食祿而徒庸庸碌碌無
所為於時與夫衎衎焉營營
焉以圖其私便是皆不恤瘝
曠之誚負秉之譏為庸俗所
punctuated: 而物正，如古所謂大人者，其上也。贊襄謀謨，黼黻政令，朝廷倚為重輕，天下繫其安危，如古所謂社稷臣者，其次也。其或當一面、守一郡、典一邑，勤勞宣於方岳，愷悌洽于閭里，如古所謂王之藩屏、民之父母者，又其次也。隨所任使，要皆殫厥心力，有益於國家、有益於生民而后可。若乃儋爵食祿，而徒庸庸碌碌、無所為於時，與夫衎衎焉、營營焉以圖其私便，是皆不恤瘝曠之誚、負乘之譏，為庸俗所
translation_en: …so that all things are rectified, like those whom the ancients called "great men"—this is the highest ideal. Assisting in counsels and plans, adorning governmental ordinances, so that the court relies on one for its weight and authority, and the empire depends on one for its security or peril, like those whom the ancients called "ministers of the altars of soil and grain"—this is the next best. Or perhaps taking charge of a regional command, governing a prefecture, or administering a district, extending one's diligent toil across the provincial administration and spreading joyful kindness throughout the villages and hamlets, like those whom the ancients called "screens and bulwarks of the king" and "parents of the people"—this is the next after that. Whatever office one is assigned to, the essential thing is that all must exhaust their mental and physical strength so as to be of benefit to the state and of benefit to the people—only then is it acceptable. As for bearing noble rank and drawing an official salary while merely being mediocre and accomplishing nothing in one's time, or complacently and busily scheming for one's own private convenience—all such men pay no heed to the reproach of neglecting their offices or the ridicule of "carrying a load while riding in a carriage," and are [scorned and]… by ordinary folk…

title: 成化十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
鄙陋而可謂士乎哉諸士子
平居讀書問學於古豪傑光
昭簡策者莫不有嚮往之心
於不肖者則相與排斥而訾
毀之矣乃今出自科目而是
錄之傳異日人亦將指其名
而議之其可不思自奮勵以
===
匹休前聞而貽科目羞哉小
錄既成敬序此於篇端為諸
士子勗
左春坊左諭德謝一夔謹序

士子勗
左春坊左諭德謝〔一夔〕謹序
punctuated:
鄙陋，而可謂士乎哉？諸士子平居讀書問學，於古豪傑光昭簡策者，莫不有嚮往之心；於不肖者，則相與排斥而訾毀之矣。乃今出自科目，而是錄之傳，異日人亦將指其名而議之，其可不思自奮勵以匹休前聞，而貽科目羞哉？小錄既成，敬序此於篇端，為諸士子勗。
左春坊左諭德謝一夔謹序。
translation_en:
…despised by ordinary folk—how could such men be called scholars? In their everyday lives, as these gentlemen read books and pursue learning, there is none who does not yearn to emulate the heroes of antiquity whose glory shines in the historical records, while together they reject and revile the unworthy. Now that they have emerged through the examination system and this record will be handed down, in days to come people will likewise point to their names and pass judgment upon them. How could they fail to reflect on rousing and exerting themselves so as to match the fine reputation of those celebrated predecessors, rather than bringing shame upon the examination system? Now that this brief record is completed, I respectfully write this preface at the head of the volume as an exhortation to the gentlemen.

Respectfully prefaced by Xie Yikui 謝一夔, Left Admonisher of the Left Secretariat of the Heir Apparent.

title: 成化十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
畏天命畏大人畏聖人之言
武王纘大王王季文王之緒壹戎衣而有
天下身不失天下之顯名尊為天子富
有四海之內宗廟饗之子孫保之武王
末受命周公成文武之德追王大王王
季上祀先公以天子之禮
文王我師也周公豈欺我哉
===
易
初筮告再三瀆瀆則不告利貞
剛上而尚賢能止健大正也
八卦而小成引而伸之觸類而長之天下
之能事畢矣
聖人以此洗心退藏於密吉凶與民同患
神以知來知以藏往其孰能與於此哉
古之聰明叡知神武而不殺者夫是以
明於天之道而察於民之故是興神物

第壹塲
四書
畏天命畏大人畏聖人之言
武王纘大王王季文王之緒壹戎衣而有
天下身不失天下之顯名尊為天子富
有四海之内宗廟饗之子孫保之武王
末受命周公成文武之德追王大王王
季上祀先公以天子之禮
文王我師也周公豈欺我哉
===
易
初筮告再三瀆瀆則不告利貞
剛上而尚賢能止健大正也
八卦而小成引而伸之觸類而長之天下
之能事畢矣
聖人以此洗心退藏於密吉凶與民同患
神以知來知以藏往其孰能與於此哉
古之聰明叡知神武而不殺者夫是以
明於天之道而察於民之故是興神物
punctuated:
第壹場

四書
畏天命，畏大人，畏聖人之言。
武王纘大王、王季、文王之緒，壹戎衣而有天下，身不失天下之顯名，尊為天子，富有四海之內，宗廟饗之，子孫保之。武王末受命，周公成文、武之德，追王大王、王季，上祀先公以天子之禮。
文王我師也，周公豈欺我哉？

易
初筮告，再三瀆，瀆則不告。利貞。
剛上而尚賢，能止健，大正也。
八卦而小成，引而伸之，觸類而長之，天下之能事畢矣。
聖人以此洗心，退藏於密，吉凶與民同患。神以知來，知以藏往，其孰能與於此哉？古之聰明叡知，神武而不殺者夫！是以明於天之道，而察於民之故，是興神物，
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books
"He stands in awe of the Mandate of Heaven; he stands in awe of great men; he stands in awe of the words of the sages."
"King Wu (Wuwang 武王) carried on the enterprise of King Tai (Taiwang 大王), King Ji (Wang Ji 王季), and King Wen (Wenwang 文王). Once he donned his armor, he came into possession of all under Heaven. In his own person he did not lose his illustrious reputation throughout the realm. His dignity was that of the Son of Heaven; his wealth was all within the四海 (Four Seas). Sacrifices were offered to him in the ancestral temple, and his descendants preserved his legacy. King Wu received the Mandate late in life; the Duke of Zhou (Zhougong 周公) brought to completion the virtue of King Wen and King Wu, posthumously conferring the title of King on King Tai and King Ji, and sacrificing to the former dukes above with the rites proper to the Son of Heaven."
"King Wen is my teacher; how could the Duke of Zhou deceive me?"

Book of Changes (Yi 易)
"At the first divination, I inform him; to repeat it a second and third time is importunity, and if he is importunate, I do not inform him. It is advantageous to be resolute and correct."
"The firm ascends and honors the worthy; it is able to halt strength—this is great rectitude."
"With the eight trigrams, the lesser completion is reached. By extending and expanding them, and by applying them to analogous cases and augmenting them, all possible undertakings under Heaven are complete."
"With these the sage cleanses his heart, retiring and storing them in secrecy; in good fortune and misfortune, he shares the anxieties of the people. Spiritual so as to know the future, wise so as to store the past—who is able to participate in this? Surely those of antiquity who were intelligent, perspicacious, and wise, possessing divine martial prowess without resorting to killing! Therefore, comprehending the Way of Heaven and examining the affairs of the people, they instituted these sacred objects…"

詩
淑人君子，其帶伊絲。其帶伊絲，其弁伊騏。
四鍭如樹，序賓以不侮。曾孫維主，酒醴維醹，酌以大斗，以祈黃耇。黃耇台背。
穆穆皇皇，宜君宜王。不愆不忘，率由舊章。威儀抑抑，德音秩秩。無怨無惡，率由群匹。
translation_en:
… in order to prepare things for the use of the people. With these the sages practiced abstinence and fasting, to render their virtue spiritual and luminous!

Classic of Documents (Shu):
"Be clear about the five punishments so as to assist the five teachings, aiming at the perfection of my government, and aiming through punishment at there being no punishment."
"I dare to respond to and extol the beneficent charge of the Son of Heaven."
"August Heaven has already committed the people of the Central Land and its territory to the former kings. Now let the King employ only virtue to harmonize and gladden and to guide and care for the deluded people, thereby gladdening the former kings who received the Mandate. Yes! Viewing things thus, our only desire is to reach to ten thousand years; may the King's sons and grandsons forever protect the people."
"When all the measures of government are harmonious, the myriad states are all at peace."

Classic of Poetry (Shi):
"The good man, the princely man—his girdle is of silk; his girdle is of silk, and his cap is ofspotted deer-skin [or dark-mottled]."
"The four arrows are as if planted; the guests are arranged according to their non-insolent demeanor. The descendant is the host; the spirits and sweet wines are rich; he pours them with a great ladle, to pray for yellow-haired old age—yellow-haired old age and a wrinkled back."
"Solemn and majestic, fit to be lord, fit to be king; neither erring nor forgetting, following the old statutes. His dignified demeanor is circumspect; his virtuous reputation is orderly; without resentment or hatred, he follows his peers."

禮記
申嚴號令命百官貴賤無不務內以會天
地之藏無有宣出
然後立之學等廣其節奏省其文采以繩
德厚律小大之稱比終始之序以象事
行
===

工入升歌三終主人獻之笙入三終主人
獻之間歌三終合樂三終工告樂備遂
出一人揚觶乃立司正焉知其能和樂
而不流也

詔誥表〔內科一道〕
translation_en:
…[note: "子" repeated from "邾子" at the end of the previous page], the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi, and the Viscount of Little Zhu attacked Zheng, and met at Xiaoyu (10th year of Duke Xiang). Prince Wu of Chu led an army to attack Zheng (18th year of Duke Xiang). The Viscount of Chu, the Marquis of Cai, the Marquis of Chen, and the Baron of Xu attacked Zheng (24th year of Duke Xiang).

Record of Rites (Liji)
Orders and commands are reiterated with strictness, charging all officials, noble and base alike, that none fail to attend to the storing of things within, so as to accord with the hoarding of Heaven and Earth, and that nothing be dispersed abroad.
Thereupon, grades of instruction are established for it; its rhythms and cadences are broadened, and its ornamental flourishes are examined, so as to measure the depth of virtue; the proportions of small and great are regulated, and the sequence of beginning and end is aligned, so as to symbolize the conduct of affairs.
Purification is the utmost degree of refined clarity; only after that can one commune with the bright spirits.
The musicians enter, ascend, and sing three pieces to their conclusion, whereupon the host presents them a cup; the reed-organ players enter and play three pieces to their conclusion, whereupon the host presents them a cup; alternating songs are performed for three pieces, and ensemble music is performed for three pieces; the musicians announce that the music is complete and then go out. One man raises the goblet, and thereupon an Overseer of Ritual (sizheng) is appointed. From this one knows that they are able to be harmonious and joyful without falling into dissipation.

Second Session
Discourse
"The superior man earnestly seeks to lead his ruler along the proper Way."

下之詞以勸其善戒其惡而冀其弼成
一代治化之盛若成湯之誕告萬方成

第叄場
策
問：自古聖帝明王之治天下，必有訓飭臣下之詞，以勸其善、戒其惡，而冀其弼成一代治化之盛。若成湯之誕告萬方，成王之訓迪百官，是已。鴻惟我宣宗章皇帝，萬機之暇，采輯東周以降人臣之善可為法、惡可為戒者，類為《歷代臣鑒》一書，用錫群臣，俾時省覽。蓋與商、周之
translation_en:
Draft an edict on behalf of Emperor Wen of the Han (漢文帝) relaxing state monopolies on profit and reducing expenditures in order to relieve the people.
Draft a mandate of appointment on behalf of the Tang dynasty appointing Pei Du (裴度) as Vice Director of the Secretariat (中書侍郎) and Jointly Manager of Affairs with the Secretariat-Chancellery (同平章事).
Draft a memorial of gratitude on behalf of Sima Guang (司馬光) of the Song dynasty for the imperial bestowal of a preface to the Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance (Zizhi tongjian 資治通鑑).

Legal Judgments
Recommending and employing officials and subofficial functionaries who have committed offenses.
Privately impressing commoners, laborers, and artisans under one's jurisdiction into service.
Diviners and occultists recklessly prognosticating misfortune and good fortune.
Dukes and Marquises privately impressing government soldiers into service.
Government authorities deliberately increasing or reducing sentences for offenses.

Third Session
Policy Questions
Question: Since antiquity, when sage emperors and enlightened kings governed the realm, they invariably issued words of instruction and admonition to their ministers and subordinates in order to encourage their goodness and warn against their evil, hoping that they would assist in accomplishing the flourishing transformative governance of an era. Such was the case when Cheng Tang (成湯) issued a grand proclamation to the myriad regions, and when King Cheng (成王) instructed and guided the hundred officials. Greatly reflecting upon how Our Emperor Xuanzong Zhang (宣宗章皇帝, the Xuande Emperor), in his leisure from the myriad affairs of state, gathered and compiled accounts of ministers from the Eastern Zhou onward whose goodness could serve as a model and whose evil could serve as a warning, categorizing them into a book entitled Mirror for Ministers of Successive Dynasties (Lidai chenjian 歷代臣鑒), which he bestowed upon the assembled ministers so that they might examine and read it from time to time—indeed, with those of the rulers of Shang and Zhou…

title: 成化十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
君訓飭之詞異世而同符其有益於臣
工大矣諸士子莊誦
聖訓盖亦有年姑舉其一二相與講明之如憂
國奉公守正不阿無中惟圖書衣衾胃
中有數萬甲兵是皆善可為法者其人
可得而悉數歟深文舞智口蜜腹劍謬
為豐亨豫大之說倡有天書雲篆之符
是皆惡可為戒者其人可得而詳言歟
四方灾變郡未及上而輒以聞與中外
===
所陳利害一切報罷者何以槩謂之善
力主和議而沮北伐之兵與密謀行軍
而為恢復之計者何以均謂之惡大臣
不當親細事而竹頭木屑之必計者果
在所當戒乎人臣貴盡言無隱而柴塩
利害之悉上者果在所當法乎方
今内外百辟服膺
聖訓而勇於為善者固多其間敢於為惡者亦
不少玆欲盡化挾姦縱私者惟忠貞之

punctuated: 君訓飭之詞，異世而同符，其有益於臣工大矣。諸士子莊誦聖訓，盖亦有年，姑舉其一二，相與講明之：如憂國奉公、守正不阿、無中惟圖書衣衾、胃中有數萬甲兵，是皆善可為法者，其人可得而悉數歟？深文舞智、口蜜腹劍、謬為豐亨豫大之說、倡有天書雲篆之符，是皆惡可為戒者，其人可得而詳言歟？四方灾變，郡未及上而輒以聞，與中外所陳利害一切報罷者，何以槩謂之善？力主和議而沮北伐之兵，與密謀行軍而為恢復之計者，何以均謂之惡？大臣不當親細事，而竹頭木屑之必計者，果在所當戒乎？人臣貴盡言無隱，而柴塩利害之悉上者，果在所當法乎？方今内外百辟，服膺聖訓而勇於為善者固多，其間敢於為惡者亦不少。玆欲盡化挾姦縱私者惟忠貞之…
translation_en: …sovereigns’ words of admonition and instruction, though from different eras, tally with one another, and their benefit to the officials is great indeed. You scholars have reverently recited the sacred instructions for some years now; let us tentatively cite one or two points to discuss and elucidate together. For instance: worrying over the state and devoting oneself to the public good; upholding rectitude without flattering; having nothing in one’s bags [? 無中, likely a print error for 橐中] save books, charts, clothes, and bedding; or having tens of thousands of armored soldiers within one’s breast [? 胃中, for 胸中]—all these are examples of the good that can serve as a model. Can the men to whom they refer be enumerated in full? Manipulating the law with harshness and cleverness; having honey on one’s lips and a sword in one’s belly; falsely advancing theories of “abundance, prosperity, ease, and greatness” (fengheng yuda); or initiating the auspices of “Heavenly Texts” in cloud-seal script—all these are examples of the evil that can serve as a warning. Can the men to whom they refer be spoken of in detail? Why is it that both reporting disasters and anomalies in the four quarters to the throne before the commanderies had even submitted their accounts, and summarily rejecting all proposals regarding advantages and disadvantages submitted from within and without the court, are alike categorized as good? Why is it that both strenuously advocating peace negotiations to obstruct a northern expedition, and secretly plotting military campaigns to plan for restoration, are equally called evil? Great ministers ought not to attend personally to trivial matters—so is one who insists on accounting even for bamboo scraps and wood shavings truly to be taken as a warning? A subject values speaking out fully without concealment—so is one who submits every detail concerning the pros and cons of firewood and salt truly to be taken as a model? At present, among the hundred officials inside and outside the capital, those who take the sacred instructions to heart and are courageous in doing good are certainly many, yet among them those who dare to do evil are also not few. If we now wish entirely to transform those who harbor treachery and indulge in selfish interests so that they cherish only loyalty and integrity…

text:
懷盡革傷仁敗德者惟循良之尚其道
何居諸士子行將效用于時其於惡可
為戒者灼知必不為矣至於善可為法
者孰在所願學歟幸盡言之以觀所志
問先儒有云寬猛相濟政是以和斯不易
之論也然考之古人言論政績有不盡
同者周禮曰刑新國用輕典刑平國用
中典刑亂國用重典盖因其時而施之
如此或者曰寬以待良民嚴以馭姦民
===
又曰撫民當寬束吏貴嚴則又因其人
而施之何歟公孫僑曰有德者能以寬
服民崔寔則曰嚴之則理寬之則亂其
言之不同又何歟由數說觀之則寬猛
相濟之論非歟然諸葛治蜀刑法峻急
裴度平蔡反其苛政何輕重異施而皆
治歟薛奎居蜀以惠稱其尹開封也則
治以嚴肅蘇頌守杭以寬稱其為京兆
也則嚴以鞭朴何前後異施而皆善歟

懷，盡革傷仁敗德者惟循良之尚，其道何居？諸士子行將效用于時，其於惡可為戒者，灼知必不為矣；至於善可為法者，孰在所願學歟？幸盡言之，以觀所志。
問：先儒有云：「寬猛相濟，政是以和。」斯不易之論也。然考之古人言論政績，有不盡同者。《周禮》曰：「刑新國用輕典，刑平國用中典，刑亂國用重典。」盖因其時而施之如此。或者曰：「寬以待良民，嚴以馭姦民。」又曰：「撫民當寬，束吏貴嚴。」則又因其人而施之，何歟？公孫僑曰：「有德者能以寬服民。」崔寔則曰：「嚴之則理，寬之則亂。」其言之不同又何歟？由數說觀之，則寬猛相濟之論非歟？然諸葛治蜀，刑法峻急；裴度平蔡，反其苛政。何輕重異施而皆治歟？薛奎居蜀以惠稱，其尹開封也，則治以嚴肅；蘇頌守杭以寬稱，其為京兆也，則嚴以鞭朴。何前後異施而皆善歟？
translation_en:
…cherish only loyalty and integrity, and utterly reform those who injure benevolence and ruin virtue so that they esteem only upright and良 [conscientious] conduct—what is the way to achieve this? You gentlemen are soon to offer your service to the age. As for the evil deeds that may serve as warnings, we clearly know you will certainly not commit them; as for the good deeds that may serve as models, which are the ones you wish to emulate? Pray state your views in full, so that we may observe your aspirations.

Question: Former Confucians had a saying [from the Zuo Commentary]: "When leniency and severity complement each other, governance is thereby harmonious." This is an immutable argument. Yet when we examine the discourses and administrative achievements of the ancients, they are not entirely identical. The Rites of Zhou (Zhouli) says: "In punishing a newly established state, use light statutes; in punishing a peaceful state, use moderate statutes; in punishing a disorderly state, use heavy statutes." This was because they applied them in accordance with the times. Some say: "Use leniency to treat good commoners, and strictness to control wicked commoners." And it is also said: "In soothing the people one ought to be lenient; in restraining subofficial functionaries it is important to be strict." Here they applied them in accordance with the persons involved—why is this? Gongsun Qiao [Zichan] said: "Only one who possesses virtue is able to subdue the people with leniency." Cui Shi, on the other hand, said: "Treat them strictly and there will be order; treat them leniently and there will be disorder." Why Again do their words differ so? Viewed in light of these several explanations, is the argument that leniency and severity complement each other wrong? Yet when Zhuge [Liang] governed Shu, his penal laws were stern and urgent; when Pei Du pacified Cai, he reversed its harsh governance. Why did they apply lightness and heaviness differently and yet both achieve order? When Xue Kui resided in Shu, he was praised for his kindness, yet when he served as Prefect of Kaifeng, he governed with strictness and solemnity; when Su Song served as Prefect of Hangzhou, he was praised for his leniency, yet when he governed Jingzhao [the capital prefecture], he was strict in using the whip and rod. Why did their earlier and later measures differ and yet both prove admirable? …

title: 成化十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
欲如僑言則有萑苻之咎如寔言則有
蒼鷹之誚如之何而後無弊也我
國家垂統于茲餘百年深仁厚澤洽于民心
而紀綱法度粲然具備猶一日也然行
之既久施為緩急寧無太過不及之弊
其所以弛張損益得無可議者乎古之
人有窮居而言天下之事者矣諸生應
賓興而來皆懷通變之才者試為我言
之以俟
君相采焉
===
問賞罰人主之大柄也賞當其功則天下
勸罰當其罪則天下懼盖理之必然者
三代而上無容議矣姑舉漢唐諸君賞
罰言之如不以舊怨而不封不以私恩
而不戮或徵以寬和或誅以殘酷高祖
宣帝賞罰之公固矣然嬖倖之侯元功
之誅與夫戶口偽增者旌之干犯之數
者誅之其亦公歟不歟用之不念仇讐

勸罰當其罪則天下懼蓋理之必然者
三代而上無容議矣姑舉漢唐諸君賞

宣帝賞罰之公固矣然雙偉之戾元功
之誅與夫戶口僞增者旌之干紀之數
者誅之其亦公歟不歟用之不念仇讐
punctuated:
欲如僑言，則有萑苻之咎；如寔言，則有蒼鷹之誚。如之何而後無弊也？我國家垂統于茲，餘百年深仁厚澤洽于民心，而紀綱法度粲然具備猶一日也。然行之既久，施為緩急寧無太過、不及之弊？其所以弛張損益，得無可議者乎？古之人有窮居而言天下之事者矣。諸生應賓興而來，皆懷通變之才者，試為我言之，以俟君相采焉。
問：賞罰，人主之大柄也。賞當其功則天下勸，罰當其罪則天下懼，盖理之必然者。三代而上，無容議矣。姑舉漢、唐諸君賞罰言之：如不以舊怨而不封，不以私恩而不戮；或徵以寬和，或誅以殘酷，高祖、宣帝賞罰之公固矣。然嬖倖之侯、元功之誅，與夫戶口偽增者旌之、干犯之數者誅之，其亦公歟，不歟？用之不念仇讐，
translation_en:
If one wishes to follow Gongsun Qiao's words, then there is the fault of bandits gathering in the reed marshes [from excessive leniency]; if one follows Cui Shi's words, then there is the ridicule of behaving like a "pale-blue hawk" [from ruthless severity]. How should one act so that there will finally be no abuses? Since our Dynasty handed down the imperial succession to the present, for over a hundred years its deep benevolence and generous grace have suffused the hearts of the people, while its guiding principles and legal institutions have remained brilliantly complete as if it were all a single day. Yet when policies have been practiced for a long time, in the urgency or relaxation of their implementation how could there not be abuses of going too far or falling short? As for the ways of relaxing or tightening, diminishing or augmenting them, could there not be matters worthy of discussion? Among the ancients there were those who lived in obscurity and yet spoke of the affairs of the world. You students, who have come in response to the call to the provincial examination, all harbor the talent for adapting to change; try to set this forth for me, so as to await selection by our Sovereign and his ministers.

Question: Rewards and punishments are the great handles of authority of the ruler of men. When rewards match merits, the empire is encouraged; when punishments match crimes, the empire stands in awe—this is truly the inevitable principle of things. Of the Three Dynasties and earlier, there is no need for discussion. Let us provisionally take up and speak of the rewards and punishments of several rulers of the Han and Tang: for instance, not withholding enfeoffment because of old resentments, and not sparing from execution because of private favor; or summoning to court for gentle leniency, and executing for残酷 cruelty—the impartiality of the rewards and punishments of Emperor Gaozu and Emperor Xuan of the Han was solid indeed. Yet enfeoffing favorites as marquises and executing men of foremost merit, as well as honoring those who falsely inflated household and population registers and executing those who repeatedly gave offense [with frank remonstrance]—were these also impartial or not? Employing men without bearing grudges against former enemies, …

title: 成化十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
斥之不私故舊討積年之叛相鯁直之
臣太宗憲宗賞罰之公然矣然佞人之
擢讜言之誅與夫事聚斂者相之詆異
端者竄之其亦公歟不歟之數君者皆
漢唐之英君誼辟而賞罰如此此治之
所繇不三代若也鴻惟
皇上自即位以來勵精圖治論功行賞而無不
稱之賞因罪施罰而無濫及之罰故治
化之盛足以媲美三代而非漢唐所可
===
及也柰何近年為將帥者或縱士卒而
濫殺無辜以要功或昵親舊而妄作功
次以申請於是無功受賞者不能無矣
欲悉疑之而不予則使邊將難於用人
以成武功欲悉予之而不疑則使奸巧
得肆欺罔以圖僥倖然則如之何而后
無弊歟典刑獄者或妄有比附而傅致
其罪或意有偏徇而高下其手於是無
罪受罰者容或有矣欲霈施矜恤則有

translation_en: …and dismissing them without showing favoritism to old acquaintances; or suppressing rebellions of many years' standing and appointing upright and outspoken ministers as chief counselors—the impartiality of rewards and punishments under Taizong and Xianzong of Tang was indeed so. Yet when flatterers were promoted and those who offered honest counsel were executed, or when men who engaged in fiscal exaction were made chief counselors and those who denounced heterodoxy were banished—were these acts also impartial, or not? These several rulers were all heroic and righteous sovereigns of the Han and Tang, yet their rewards and punishments were like this; this is the reason why their governance did not match that of the Three Dynasties. We humbly reflect that since His Majesty ascended the throne, he has applied himself with vigor to governance, assessing merit to bestow rewards so that there is no reward undeserved, and meting out punishments according to the crime so that there is no punishment excessively applied. Thus the flourishing of his transformative governance is worthy to rival the beauty of the Three Dynasties and is beyond what the Han and Tang could attain. Why is it, then, that in recent years those who serve as generals and commanders sometimes give free rein to their soldiers to wantonly slaughter the innocent in order to claim merit, or show partiality to relatives and old acquaintances by falsely fabricating records of merit for submission? As a result, it has been impossible to avoid having men who receive rewards without merit. If one wishes to suspect them all and withhold rewards, it makes it difficult for frontier commanders to employ men to achieve military accomplishments; if one wishes to grant them all without suspicion, it allows the deceitful and cunning to indulge in fraud and deception in pursuit of undeserved fortune. How, then, can this be handled so that there are no abuses? Those in charge of penal cases and prisons sometimes arbitrarily draw analogies to statutes to fabricate and fix a person's guilt, or harbor partiality in their intentions and manipulate the sentences up or down; as a result, there may well be those who suffer punishment without guilt. If one wishes to lavishly bestow compassion and leniency, it…

title: 成化十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
戾於勿誤之訓欲如所論列則有乖於
好生之德然則如之何而后斯中歟二
者必有至當之論二三子幸明以告我
我將轉而聞於
上
問儒者之用大矣施之政事則曰儒吏施
之軍旅則曰儒將三代而上皐夔即吏
也伊呂亦將也何嘗岐而二耶後世吏
以刀筆為事而三尺是持將以馳射為
===
能而一丁不識於是皆與儒為二矣考
之載籍如絃歌之化武城彈琴而治單
父固儒吏也彼興學於蜀而文風比齊
魯經學飾吏而非俗吏所及守弘農而
虎北渡河刺潮陽而鱷不為暴者亦可
謂儒吏歟亦有優劣之可言歟他如論
湯旱為桀之餘烈以天變為神恠不語
者皆世所謂儒也其為吏而奸欺乃爾
儒者固如是歟才全文武而北伐無功

punctuated:
戾於「勿誤」之訓；欲如所論列，則有乖於「好生」之德。然則如之何而后斯中歟？二者必有至當之論，二三子幸明以告我，我將轉而聞於上。

問：儒者之用大矣。施之政事，則曰儒吏；施之軍旅，則曰儒將。三代而上，皐、夔即吏也，伊、呂亦將也，何嘗岐而二耶？後世吏以刀筆為事，而三尺是持；將以馳射為能，而一丁不識，於是皆與儒為二矣。考之載籍，如絃歌之化武城，彈琴而治單父，固儒吏也。彼興學於蜀而文風比齊、魯，經學飾吏而非俗吏所及，守弘農而虎北渡河，刺潮陽而鱷不為暴者，亦可謂儒吏歟？亦有優劣之可言歟？他如論湯旱為桀之餘烈，以天變為神恠不語者，皆世所謂儒也，其為吏而奸欺乃爾，儒者固如是歟？才全文武而北伐無功，
translation_en:
…run counter to the precept of "making no error [in judicial matters]"; yet if we wish to proceed strictly according to the charges as presented, it would violate the virtue of "cherishing life." How, then, is the proper mean to be attained? On both of these matters there must be a thoroughly sound discourse. Gentlemen, please explain it clearly to me, and I shall in turn report it to the Throne.

Question: Great indeed is the utility of Confucian scholars! When applied to civil governance, they are called "scholar-officials" (ruli); when applied to military affairs, they are called "scholar-generals" (rujiang). In the Three Dynasties and earlier, Gao Yao and Kui were themselves administrative officials, and Yi Yin and Lü Shang were also generals—when were these roles ever split in two? In later ages, administrative officials made knife-and-brush clerical work their business, upholding only the three-foot bamboo slips of the law; generals took riding and archery as their sole capability, without knowing a single written character. Thus both became separated from Confucian scholarship.

Examining the historical records, transforming Wucheng through the music of stringed instruments and singing [Ziyou], and governing Shanfu by playing the zither [Zijian], were certainly the deeds of scholar-officials. What of those who promoted schools in Shu so that its literary culture rivaled Qi and Lu [Wen Weng], who adorned administrative service with classical learning beyond the reach of vulgar clerks [Ni Kuan / Gongsun Hong], who served as Grand守 (Governor) of Hongnong when tigers crossed the Yellow River to the north [Liu Kun], and who served as Prefect of Chaoyang when crocodiles ceased their depredations [Han Yu]—can they also be called scholar-officials? And can their relative merits and shortcomings be evaluated? As for others—such as the one who argued that King Tang's drought was the lingering heat of King Jie's tyranny [Gongsun Hong], or the one who dismissed celestial anomalies on the grounds that the Master did not speak of prodigies [Zhang Yu]—all were what the world called Confucians; yet as officials they were so deceitful and treacherous! Are true Confucians really like this?

To possess complete civil and military talent so that the northern expedition succeeded without having to claim martial merit [Jifu],…

title: 成化十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
說禮敦詩而一戰伯晉固儒將也彼雅
歌投壺不忘俎豆緩帶輕裘不被戎服
出師有表而以復漢為心左傳有癖而
收平吳之績者亦可謂儒將歟亦有得
失之可議歟他如作文賦而有河橋之
敗學春秋而有陳濤之奔者亦世所謂
儒也其為將而僨事如此儒者果無用
歟方
今科貢取士百辟皆儒而功利之徒不能無
===
武學有制介胄知書而文武之才猶未
見伊欲吏先教化將務韜畧一洗習俗
之弊而使儒者之效暴於天下是必有
道矣諸士子以儒為業講之有素其悉
陳之以觀明古識今之學
問
朝廷設科取士而策以時務者盖欲觀士子
有用之實學也時務可言者多矣姑舉
一二切於今日者試相與商確之古者

說禮敦詩而一戰伯晉國儒將也彼雅
歌投壷不忘俎豆綏帶輕裘不被戎服
出師有表而以復漢為心左傳有癖而
收平吳之績者亦可謂儒將歟亦有得
失之可議歟他如作文賦而有河橋之
敗學春秋而有陳濤之犇者亦世所謂
儒也其為將而憤事如此儒者果無用
歟方
今科貢取士百辟皆儒而功利之徒不能無
===
武學有制介胄知書而文武之才猶未
見伊欲吏先教化將務韜畧一洗習俗
之弊而使儒者之效暴於天下是必有
道矣諸士子以儒為業講之有素其悉
陳之以觀明古識今之學
問
朝廷設科取士而策以時務者盖欲觀士子
有用之實學也時務可言者多矣姑舉
一二切於今日者試相與商確之古者
punctuated:
說《禮》敦《詩》而一戰伯晉，固儒將也；彼雅歌投壺、不忘俎豆，緩帶輕裘、不被戎服，出師有表、而以復漢為心，《左傳》有癖、而收平吳之績者，亦可謂儒將歟？亦有得失之可議歟？他如作《文賦》而有河橋之敗，學《春秋》而有陳濤之奔者，亦世所謂儒也，其為將而僨事如此，儒者果無用歟？方今科貢取士，百辟皆儒，而功利之徒不能無；武學有制，介胄知書，而文武之才猶未見。伊欲吏先教化，將務韜畧，一洗習俗之弊，而使儒者之效暴於天下，是必有道矣。諸士子以儒為業，講之有素，其悉陳之，以觀明古識今之學。

問：朝廷設科取士，而策以時務者，盖欲觀士子有用之實學也。時務可言者多矣，姑舉一二切於今日者，試相與商確之。古者
translation_en:
… [and he who] delighted in the Rites and esteemed the Odes, winning hegemony for Jin in a single battle, were indeed Confucian generals. As for those who sang elegant songs and played the pitch-pot game while never forgetting ritual vessels, who wore loose sashes and light furs instead of donning military attire, who presented memorials on marching forth to campaign with hearts set on restoring the Han, or who had an obsession with the Zuo Commentary (Zuozhuan) and achieved the merit of pacifying Wu—can they also be called Confucian generals? Are there also successes and failures among them that can be discussed? What of others, such as he who composed the Rhapsody on Literature (Wen fu) yet suffered defeat at Heqiao, or he who studied the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) yet fled in rout at Chentao? They too were what the world calls Confucians; yet when serving as generals they ruined affairs like this—are Confucians really of no use?

At present, scholars are selected through the examinations and tribute-student systems, so that all officials are Confucians, yet there is no lack of men bent on功利 (utility and profit); the Military Schools have their established regulations, so that armored soldiers know books, yet talent combining the civil and the military has still not been seen. If we wish civil officials to put moral transformation first and generals to devote themselves to strategic arts, completely washing away the abuses of entrenched custom and making the efficacy of Confucians manifest throughout the realm, there must certainly be a way to do this. You gentlemen make Confucian learning your profession and have long studied these matters; set forth your views in full, so that we may observe your learning in understanding antiquity and recognizing the needs of the present.

Question: When the court establishes examinations to select scholars and tests them with policy questions on current affairs, it is because it wishes to observe the scholars' practical and useful learning. There are many current affairs that could be discussed; let us tentatively raise one or two that are urgent for today, and try to deliberate on them together. In antiquity, …

title: 成化十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
鄉舉里選賓興賢能固未始限其人數
也今科舉取士不論人才之多寡一惟
解額之是遵數有未盈雖庸劣在所必
取數苟充足雖俊傑亦所必棄茲欲言
之于
上而不解額之拘則任情濫取之患又有不可
勝言者矣果何法得其要歟古者建官
惟賢位事惟能固未嘗論其年資也今
銓部選官以歷年久近為轉遷以名姓
===
先後而銓注年限未至雖英才亦不庸
資歷既深雖駑鈍亦必予茲欲請之于
朝而不年限之論則奔競躁進之弊尤有不
可紀極者矣果何道得其善歟古者三
年耕則餘一年之食積三十年之久雖
有水旱灾傷民無菜色今天下郡邑皆
設社倉似足以為備荒之策矣何一旦
小遇水旱之灾輒有請發京儲之疏欲
靳之而不發歟則有乖一視同仁之心

惟賢位事惟能固未嘗論其年資也今
銓部選官以歷年久近為轉遷以名姓
===
先後而銓注年限未至雖英才亦不庸
資歷既深雖駑鈍亦必予茲欲請之于
朝而不年限之論則奔競躁進之弊尤有不
可紀極者矣果何道得其善歟古者三
年耕則餘一年之食積三十年之久雖
有水旱災傷民無菜色今天下郡邑皆
設社倉似足以為備荒之策矣何一旦
小遇水旱之災輙有請發京儲之疏欲
靳之而不發歟則有乖一視同仁之心
punctuated: 鄉舉里選，賓興賢能，固未始限其人數也。今科舉取士，不論人才之多寡，一惟解額之是遵。數有未盈，雖庸劣在所必取；數苟充足，雖俊傑亦所必棄。茲欲言之于上，而不解額之拘，則任情濫取之患，又有不可勝言者矣。果何法得其要歟？古者建官惟賢，位事惟能，固未嘗論其年資也。今銓部選官，以歷年久近為轉遷，以名姓先後而銓注。年限未至，雖英才亦不庸；資歷既深，雖駑鈍亦必予。茲欲請之于朝，而不年限之論，則奔競躁進之弊，尤有不可紀極者矣。果何道得其善歟？古者三年耕則餘一年之食，積三十年之久，雖有水旱灾傷，民無菜色。今天下郡邑皆設社倉，似足以為備荒之策矣。何一旦小遇水旱之灾，輒有請發京儲之疏？欲靳之而不發歟，則有乖一視同仁之心；
translation_en:
… districts recommended and villages selected, presenting the worthy and the able as guests of the state, without ever initially setting a limit on their numbers. Today, in selecting scholars through the civil service examinations, regardless of the abundance or scarcity of talent, one strictly adheres only to the provincial quota. If the number has not yet been filled, even the mediocre and inferior must be selected; if the number is already met, even the outstanding and brilliant must be rejected. Should we now wish to propose to the Emperor that we not be bound by the quota, the evil of arbitrary and indiscriminate selection would be beyond description. By what method, indeed, can the essential balance be attained?

In antiquity, offices were established only for the worthy, and duties were assigned only to the capable, without ever considering their seniority. Today, when the Ministry of Personnel selects officials, transfers and promotions are based on the length of years served, and appointments are made according to the order of names on the roster. If the required term of years has not been reached, even a brilliant talent is not employed; once seniority is sufficiently deep, even a dullard is 반드시 granted a post. Should we now wish to petition the Court not to base decisions on length of service, the abuse of scrambling for advancement and impatiently seeking promotion would be utterly boundless. By what way, indeed, can the best course be attained?

In antiquity, three years of耕種 (plowing) yielded a surplus of one year's food; accumulating this over thirty years, even if there were disasters of flood or drought, the people did not have the famished complexion of those eating only wild greens. Today, prefectures and counties throughout the empire have all established community granaries, which would seem sufficient as a measure for famine relief. Why is it that as soon as they encounter a minor disaster of flood or drought, there are immediately memorials requesting the distribution of the capital's grain reserves? If we wish to withhold them and not distribute them, that would run counter to the benevolent heart that regards all equally; …

title: 成化十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
欲隨所請而發之歟則不惟京儲有限
抑且有轉徙輓運之勞茲欲使郡邑之
粟自足賑恤其民夫豈無其法歟古者
鄉遂丘甸皆有甲兵故雖有外侮自足
以捍禦之今沿邊衛所各屯重兵宜足
以為禦侮之計矣何一旦卒遇寇虜之
侵即有乞調大軍之請欲拒之而不遣
歟則恐遺一方生靈之害欲如所請而
調撥歟則不惟裹糧跋涉抑恐有老師
===
挫銳之患茲欲俾邊衛之兵自足保障
一方是豈無其道歟此皆今日時務之
切者諸士子強學待問必有善處之術
言及之而不言聖人所不取也
alt_text:
欲隨所請而發之歟則不惟京儲有限
抑且有轉徙輓運之勞茲欲使郡邑之
粟自足賑卹其民夫豈無其法歟古者
鄉遂丘甸皆有甲兵故雖有外侮自足
以捍禦之今沿邊衛所各屯重兵宜足
以為禦侮之計矣何一旦卒遇寇虜之
侵即有乞調大軍之請欲拒之而不遣
歟則恐遺一方生靈之害欲如所請而
調撥歟則不惟累糧跋涉抑恐有老師
挫鋭之患茲欲俾邊衛之兵自足保障
一方是豈無其道歟此皆今日時務之
切者諸士子殚學待問必有善處之術
言及之而不言聖人所不取也
punctuated:
欲隨所請而發之歟？則不惟京儲有限，抑且有轉徙輓運之勞。茲欲使郡邑之粟自足賑恤其民，夫豈無其法歟？
古者鄉遂丘甸皆有甲兵，故雖有外侮，自足以捍禦之。今沿邊衛所各屯重兵，宜足以為禦侮之計矣；何一旦卒遇寇虜之侵，即有乞調大軍之請？欲拒之而不遣歟？則恐遺一方生靈之害。欲如所請而調撥歟？則不惟裹糧跋涉，抑恐有老師挫銳之患。茲欲俾邊衛之兵自足保障一方，是豈無其道歟？
此皆今日時務之切者，諸士子強學待問，必有善處之術。言及之而不言，聖人所不取也。
translation_en:
…Or should we release them whenever requested? Then not only are the capital reserves finite, there would also be the hardship of transport and haulage. If we now wish to make the grain of the prefectures and counties sufficient in itself to relieve their own people, can it be that there is no method for this?

In antiquity, the districts, outskirts, hills, and tracts (xiang, sui, qiu, and dian) all had armored soldiers; thus, even when there was foreign aggression, they were sufficient in themselves to fend it off. Today, the Guards and Battalions along the frontier each station heavy forces, which ought to suffice as a plan for repelling aggression. Why is it that the moment they suddenly encounter an incursion by bandits or northern caitiffs, there are immediately requests begging for the dispatch of the main armies? Should we refuse them and send none? Then one fears leaving the living souls of an entire region to suffer harm. Or should we transfer and deploy troops as requested? Then not only must they pack rations and trek over land and water, one also fears the danger of exhausting the army and blunting its fighting edge. If we now wish to make the soldiers of the frontier Guards sufficient in themselves to protect an entire region, can it be that there is no way to achieve this?

These are all urgent matters of current affairs today. You gentlemen have striven in your studies while awaiting questioning, and must possess the art of dealing with them well. When the occasion to speak of something arises and yet one does not speak, that is what the Sage does not approve.

title: 成化十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
第壹塲
四書
畏天命畏大人畏聖人之言
張烶
同考試官教諭李批題本平易而塲中佳作不
多見是篇理到而詞工宜録出以式来學
同考試官教諭張批知畏天命則不得不畏大
人聖言集註明矣作者多體認不真是篇析理詳
明措詞典雅讀之令人心目豁然
===
考試官修撰鄭批詞理明暢
考試官左諭德謝批得集註本㫖
君子畏夫理之賦於己者而又畏夫理之所當畏者
蓋天命在己唯君子知而畏之也大人聖言皆天命
之所當畏者君子又烏得不畏之哉聖人言此以勉
人厥㫖深矣且夫天之生人必賦之理以為性性之
所在天命之所在也人知而畏之者鮮矣君子人歟
知斯理為天命之性不畏則棄天矣必兢兢戒謹于
以存之於未發之時不啻若介圭之執惟恐其弗克

第壹塲

四書

「畏天命，畏大人，畏聖人之言。」
張烶
同考試官教諭李批：題本平易，而塲中佳作不多見。是篇理到而詞工，宜録出以式来學。
同考試官教諭張批：知畏天命，則不得不畏大人、聖言，《集註》明矣。作者多體認不真，是篇析理詳明，措詞典雅，讀之令人心目豁然。
考試官修撰鄭批：詞理明暢。
考試官左諭德謝批：得《集註》本㫖。

君子畏夫理之賦於己者，而又畏夫理之所當畏者。蓋天命在己，唯君子知而畏之也。大人、聖言，皆天命之所當畏者，君子又烏得不畏之哉？聖人言此以勉人，厥㫖深矣。且夫天之生人，必賦之理以為性，性之所在，天命之所在也，人知而畏之者鮮矣。君子人歟，知斯理為天命之性，不畏則棄天矣。必兢兢戒謹，于以存之於未發之時，不啻若介圭之執，惟恐其弗克…
translation_en:
First Session

The Four Books

"He stands in awe of the Mandate of Heaven; he stands in awe of great men; he stands in awe of the words of the sages." [Analects 16.8]

Zhang Ting 張烶

Comment by Associate Examiner, Instructor Li 李: The topic itself is plain and straightforward, yet fine compositions on it were rarely seen in the examination compound. In this essay, the reasoning hits the mark and the phrasing is skillful; it ought to be copied and published to serve as a model for future students.
Comment by Associate Examiner, Instructor Zhang 張: That once one knows to stand in awe of the Mandate of Heaven, one cannot but stand in awe of great men and the words of the sages, is already made clear in the Collected Commentaries (Jizhu 集註). Most writers fail to grasp this with genuine personal realization. This essay analyzes the principle in detail and with clarity, and its diction is refined and elegant; reading it opens up the mind and eyes.
Comment by Examiner, Senior Compiler Zheng 鄭: The phrasing and reasoning are clear and fluent.
Comment by Examiner, Left Admonisher Xie 謝: It captures the fundamental purport of the Collected Commentaries.

The superior man stands in awe of the principle endowed in himself, and therefore also stands in awe of that which, by principle, ought to be held in awe. For the Mandate of Heaven resides within oneself, and only the superior man knows it and stands in awe of it. Great men and the words of the sages are both things that, by the Mandate of Heaven, ought to be held in awe—how then could the superior man not stand in awe of them? In speaking thus to encourage men, the sage's purport was profound indeed.

Moreover, when Heaven gives birth to man, it necessarily endows him with principle to form his nature. Where one's nature resides is where the Mandate of Heaven resides; yet few are those who know it and stand in awe of it. Is the superior man not such a person? Knowing that this principle is the nature conferred by the Mandate of Heaven, he realizes that not to stand in awe of it is to abandon Heaven. Therefore, he is necessarily cautious and apprehensive, thereby preserving it before feelings are aroused—no less than if he were holding a great jade tablet (jiegui 介圭), fearing only that he might be unable to…

title: 成化十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
也知吾性為帝降之衷不畏則褻天矣必慄慄恐懼
于以保之於至靜之頃不啻若盤水之奉惟恐其或
傾也如是則付畀之重可以奉承之而不失矣君子
既知畏天命則於大人聖言之所當畏者烏能已乎
盖大人德位俱尊天命之所存也君子則恭敬而景
仰之在坐必作過之必趨何敢狎慢之乎畏大人政
所以畏天命也聖人之言布在方冊天命之所發也
君子則莊誦而佩服之信之如蓍龜遵之如指南焉
敢戲玩之乎畏聖言亦所以畏天命也天命之所在
===
君子之所畏也此君子所以為君子也歟雖然三畏
者君子脩己之誠當然也下文又曰小人不知天命
而不畏也狎大人侮聖人之言盖其不務脩身誠己
則何畏之有噫一畏不畏之間而君子小人所由分
然則學者其可忽諸
武王纘太王王季文王之緒壹戎衣而有天下
身不失天下之顯名尊為天子富有四海之
內宗廟饗之子孫保之武王末受命周公成
文武之德追王大王王季上祀先公以天子

君子之所畏也此君子所以為君子也歟雖然三畏
者君子脩已之誠當然也下文又曰小人不知天命
而不畏也狎大人侮聖人之言盖其不務脩身誠已
則何畏之有噫一畏不畏之間而君子小人所由分
然則學者其可忽諸
武王纘太王王季文王之緒壹戎衣而有天下
身不失天下之顯名尊為天子富有四海之

文武之德追王大王王季上祀先公以天子
punctuated:
也；知吾性為帝降之衷，不畏則褻天矣，必慄慄恐懼，于以保之於至靜之頃，不啻若盤水之奉，惟恐其或傾也。如是，則付畀之重可以奉承之而不失矣。君子既知畏天命，則於大人、聖言之所當畏者，烏能已乎？盖大人德位俱尊，天命之所存也；君子則恭敬而景仰之，在坐必作，過之必趨，何敢狎慢之乎？畏大人，政所以畏天命也。聖人之言，布在方冊，天命之所發也；君子則莊誦而佩服之，信之如蓍龜，遵之如指南，焉敢戲玩之乎？畏聖言，亦所以畏天命也。天命之所在，君子之所畏也，此君子所以為君子也歟！雖然，三畏者，君子脩己之誠當然也。下文又曰：「小人不知天命而不畏也，狎大人，侮聖人之言。」盖其不務脩身誠己，則何畏之有？噫！一畏不畏之間，而君子、小人所由分，然則學者其可忽諸？

… it; knowing that our human nature is the moral sense conferred by the Lord on High, not to stand in awe of it would be to profane Heaven, and so he inevitably trembles in fearful apprehension in order to protect it in moments of utmost stillness—no less than if he were holding up a basin of water, fearing only that it might tip over. Being thus, the heavy charge entrusted to him can be reverently upheld without being lost. Since the noble man knows to stand in awe of the Mandate of Heaven, how could he stop short when it comes to great men and the words of the sages, which ought also to be held in awe? For great men are exalted in both virtue and rank, and in them the Mandate of Heaven resides; the noble man therefore treats them with respectful reverence and looks up to them in admiration—when seated he inevitably rises at their approach, and when passing them he inevitably hastens his step; how would he dare be familiar with or slight them? To stand in awe of great men is precisely how one stands in awe of the Mandate of Heaven. The words of the sages are set forth on wooden tablets and bamboo slips, and are that through which the Mandate of Heaven is expressed; the noble man therefore solemnly recites them and takes them to heart, trusting them like yarrow stalks and tortoise shells and following them like a south-pointing carriage; how would he dare make sport of or trifle with them? To stand in awe of the words of the sages is likewise how one stands in awe of the Mandate of Heaven. Wherever the Mandate of Heaven resides, there the noble man stands in awe—is this not what makes the noble man a noble man? Even so, these three things held in awe are what naturally follow from the noble man's sincerity in cultivating himself. The text below goes on to say: "The petty man does not know the Mandate of Heaven and does not stand in awe of it; he is familiar with great men and scoffs at the words of the sages." For since he does not devote himself to cultivating his person and making himself sincere, what awe could he possibly have? Alas! Between standing in awe and not standing in awe lies the very division between the noble man and the petty man; how, then, can scholars afford to neglect this?

"King Wu continued the enterprise of King Tai, Wang Ji, and King Wen. Once he donned armor, he possessed the empire; in his own person he did not lose an illustrious name throughout the world; in honor he was the Son of Heaven, and in wealth he possessed all within the four seas; in the ancestral temple sacrifices were offered to him, and his descendants preserved his line. Associate Examiner, Instructor Yuan 原, comments: In the examination hall, those who wrote on this topic were mostly verbose and vague, tiresome to read. This essay grasps the meaning genuinely and phrases it concisely and clearly; no one without long-standing, thorough study could achieve this.
Associate Examiner, Director of Studies Hu 胡, comments: This concerns the greatness of King Wu and the Duke of Zhou in carrying on the intentions and continuing the affairs of their predecessors. Most essays were blind to this meaning, whereas this essay captures it; moreover, its phrasing is concise and its principle clear—a fine piece of work.
Examiner, Senior Compiler Zheng 鄭, comments: The passage topic is long, yet no words are wasted; this must be the work of a skilled hand.
Examiner, Left Admonisher Xie 謝, comments: The principle is clear and the phrasing concise, beyond the reach of an immature brush.

The former sage continued the enterprise of his predecessors and brought the flourishing of meritorious achievement to its utmost; the latter sage inherited the virtue of his predecessors and exalted the canons of posthumous veneration—both were great in carrying on and continuing the work of their forefathers. Now, in filial piety there is nothing greater than carrying on the intentions and continuing the affairs of one's predecessors. Looking at the deeds of the two sages, the greatness of their carrying on and continuing can be seen. The eighteenth chapter of the Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong) quotes the words of the Master to this effect.

Let us first speak of it in terms of the deeds of King Wu: King Tai and King Ji laid the foundation and toiled for the house, and King Wen possessed two-thirds of all under Heaven; yet did not the continuation of their enterprise await King Wu? Thereupon, once he donned armor, all under Heaven was thereby brought to great stability; complying with Heaven and responding to men, his illustrious name was thereby never lost. Honored as the Son of Heaven, there was not a single person who was not his subject; possessing the wealth of all within the four seas, there was not a foot of land that was not his own. Above, the ancestral temple enjoyed his sacrifices, so his achievements shed glory upon his ancestors; below, his descendants were able to preserve his enterprise, so his patrimony was handed down to posterity. How great was King Wu's carrying on and continuing!

… [in the time of King Wen, the] world was not yet unified, so he did not dare to institute ritual forms; and when King Wu received the Mandate in his old age, he had no leisure to establish the ritual system. Did not the means of bringing their virtue to completion rest with the Duke of Zhou? Thereupon, extending the intentions of Kings Wen and Wu back to the origins of the royal enterprise, he posthumously honored Taiwang as King Tai and Jili as King Ji, and thereby the virtue of Kings Wen and Wu was brought to completion. Further extending the intentions of King Tai and King Ji back into the boundless past, from Zugan upward all the way to Hou Ji, he sacrificed to them all with the rites of the Son of Heaven, and thereby the intentions of King Tai and King Ji were comforted. How great, too, was the Duke of Zhou's continuation and carrying forward! Our Master recounted these things in order to instruct others; profound indeed was his meaning.

Moreover, if we examine the next chapter, it further says: "Were not King Wu and the Duke of Zhou men of far-reaching filial piety! Now filial piety is skillfully continuing the intentions of one's forebears and skillfully carrying forward their undertakings." This picks up from the present chapter, and as for what is called continuing intentions and carrying forward undertakings, what could be greater than this? This is why the filial piety of King Wu and the Duke of Zhou was universally praised throughout the world. How fitting that Master Zisi cited this to illustrate the greatness of the Way's wide-reaching application!

"King Wen is my teacher; how could the Duke of Zhou deceive me?"

translation_en:
…It deserves to be placed high among the selections.

Examiner Senior Compiler Zheng comments: By basing the argument on the goodness of human nature, it grasps the main point.

Examiner Left Admonisher Xie comments: The entire essay is well-developed and fluent.

When a worthy recites the words of a later sage and sighs that those words do not deceive him, it is because he regards the former sage as certainly worthy of emulation. Indeed, human nature is universally good, and therefore sagehood can be reached through learning. Since the Duke of Zhou took King Wen as someone who could be taken as a teacher, how could Gongming Yi not recite his words and sigh that they did not deceive him?

In the past, Gongming Yi's meaning was as if to say: The Duke of Zhou had a saying that in being a ruler and practicing benevolence, and in being a subject and practicing reverence, King Wen as a sage certainly reached the ultimate peak; yet are not benevolence and reverence models for me to imitate? In being a father and practicing kindness, and in being a son and practicing filiality, King Wen in fulfilling the way of humanity certainly rested in the highest good; yet are not kindness and filiality standards for me to follow?

That the Duke of Zhou spoke in this way was truly because sages and ordinary folk share the same nature, and between antiquity and the present there are not two Ways. King Wen had this nature, and I too have this nature; if I can take him as my model without slackening, then the benevolence and reverence of King Wen can be gradually attained. The words of the Duke of Zhou are truly the most fitting of words. Supposing human nature had both good and evil, and the sage and the foolish could not be altered, would the Duke of Zhou have been willing to make such a statement to deceive us men of later generations? I follow this Way, and King Wen also followed this Way; if I can hold to his standard without losing it, then the kindness and filiality of King Wen can be reached by striving. The discourse of the Duke of Zhou is truly an unalterable discourse. Supposing the Way had two different ends, and antiquity and the present were not the same, would the Duke of Zhou have been willing to put forth this discourse to mislead us men of later generations?

Since Gongming Yi's words were like this, it can be known that human nature is universally good. How fitting it was that Mencius (Meng Ke) cited them in order to resolve the doubts of the Crown Prince of Teng! Furthermore…

title: 成化十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
□者發蒙之道而正者養蒙之道也非彖易聖人明
其占以示人其孰能知之昔文王係蒙卦之辭謂夫
人之蒙昧不可不有以發之而發之之道可無節乎
如筮者明則人為蒙而求於我矣我則於其致精一
之意者告之有初筮之誠者發之而再三煩瀆者則
不告也筮者暗則我為蒙而求於人矣我則致精一
以扣之極誠意以求之而不可有再三之瀆也發人
者當酌可否之宜發於人者當致求道之篤此蒙之
所以亨歟然蒙既發矣尤不可不有以養之而養之
===
之道可不以其正乎故明者之養蒙也宜示之以仁
義之道授之以聖賢之學于以陶鎔其德性而異端
邪說不可以罔人也蒙者之自養也宜仁義之道是
行聖賢之學是學于以涵養其良心而淫辭詖行不
可以自陷也養人者必以正自養者亦以正此蒙之
所以利歟彖易聖人因占以示人厥旨深矣抑考乾
坤之後繼之以屯蒙屯之彖曰利建侯以君道言也
蒙曰初筮告曰利貞以師道言也天地定位人物肇
生而繼天立極之責舍君師其誰與聖人序易彖易

punctuated: □者，發蒙之道；而正者，養蒙之道也。非彖《易》聖人明其占以示人，其孰能知之？昔文王係《蒙》卦之辭，謂夫人之蒙昧，不可不有以發之；而發之之道，可無節乎？如筮者明，則人為蒙而求於我矣。我則於其致精一之意者告之，有初筮之誠者發之，而再三煩瀆者則不告也。筮者暗，則我為蒙而求於人矣。我則致精一以扣之，極誠意以求之，而不可有再三之瀆也。發人者當酌可否之宜，發於人者當致求道之篤，此《蒙》之所以亨歟！然蒙既發矣，尤不可不有以養之；而養之之道，可不以其正乎？故明者之養蒙也，宜示之以仁義之道，授之以聖賢之學，于以陶鎔其德性，而異端邪說不可以罔人也。蒙者之自養也，宜仁義之道是行，聖賢之學是學，于以涵養其良心，而淫辭詖行不可以自陷也。養人者必以正，自養者亦以正，此《蒙》之所以利歟！彖《易》聖人因占以示人，厥旨深矣。抑考《乾》、《坤》之後，繼之以《屯》、《蒙》。《屯》之彖曰「利建侯」，以君道言也；《蒙》曰「初筮告」，曰「利貞」，以師道言也。天地定位，人物肇生，而繼天立極之責，舍君師其誰與？聖人序《易》、彖《易》
translation_en:
… [restraint?], is the way of enlightening the ignorant; and what is correct is the way of nurturing the ignorant. Were it not for the sage who wrote the Judgment of the Changes (Yi) clarifying its divination to instruct people, who could know this?

In antiquity, when King Wen attached the words to the Meng [Youthful Folly / Ignorance] hexagram, he considered that when people are in a state of ignorance, one cannot fail to have a means to enlighten them; yet in the way of enlightening them, how could there be no restraint? If the diviner is enlightened, then others are ignorant and seek from me. I then inform those who bring a focused and single-minded intent, and enlighten those who possess the sincerity of a first divination, whereas to those who pester and disrespectfully repeat their inquiries a second and third time, I give no answer. If the diviner is in the dark, then I am ignorant and seek from others. I then bring a focused and single-minded intent to inquire of them, and exhaust my utmost sincerity in seeking from them, and must not commit the disrespect of repeating inquiries a second and third time. He who enlightens others ought to weigh the appropriateness of whether to answer or not, and he who is enlightened by others ought to apply earnestness in seeking the Way—is this not why Meng has "success" (heng)?

Yet once ignorance has been enlightened, it is even more imperative not to fail to have a means to nurture it; and in the way of nurturing it, how could one not do so with what is correct? Therefore, when the enlightened person nurtures the ignorant, he should show them the way of humanity and righteousness, and impart to them the learning of the sages and worthies, thereby molding and refining their moral nature, while heterodox ways and perverse doctrines must not be used to deceive others. When the ignorant person nurtures himself, he should practice the way of humanity and righteousness, and study the learning of the sages and worthies, thereby nourishing his innate good conscience, while extravagant words and biased deeds must not be allowed to ensnare himself. He who nurtures others must do so with correctness, and he who nurtures himself must also do so with correctness—is this not why Meng is "favorable" (li)?

The sage who wrote the Judgment of the Changes used divination to instruct people; his meaning is profound indeed! Moreover, if we examine how after Qian [The Creative] and Kun [The Receptive] there follow Zhun [Difficulty at the Beginning] and Meng [Youthful Folly]: the Judgment of Zhun says "favorable for establishing feudal lords," which speaks in terms of the Way of the Ruler; Meng says "at the first divination, he informs" and says "favorable to be firm and correct," which speaks in terms of the Way of the Teacher. When heaven and earth set their positions, and human beings and myriad things first came into life, as for the responsibility of continuing Heaven's work and establishing the supreme standard—if one sets aside the ruler and the teacher, to whom else could it fall? The sage's intent in ordering the Changes and writing the Judgments of the Changes…

translation_en:
… the meaning of [sequencing the Changes and writing the Judgments on the Changes] is profound and subtle indeed!

"In the eight trigrams it is completed on a small scale. Drawing this out and extending it, touching on like categories and expanding them, all possible undertakings under heaven are fulfilled."
Zhang Xu 张旭.
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Li 李: Determining good and ill fortune is the "possible undertaking" of the Book of Changes (Yi 易); when scholars today point to this as referring to human affairs, they are mistaken. This essay alone shows real insight, which no one without a deep grasp of principle could achieve. It deserves to be placed first in this examination ward.
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Zhang 張: Among those in the examination compound who wrote on this topic, most lacked clear insight on the phrase "possible undertakings," quite missing the original purport. Looking for one whose explanation of principle is precise and pertinent and whose phrasing is fluent and clear, only this essay is to be found. It ought to be transcribed for publication as a model for later students.
Comment by Examiner Senior Compiler Zheng 鄭: Able to avoid being misled by the prevailing interpretations—surely one who has devoted his mind to the fundamentals.
Comment by Examiner Left Admonisher Xie 謝: Only when it is as concise and clean as this is it a true exposition of the Changes.

When the lines are completed through nine transformations, the inner trigram of the Changes is established; when the transformations are carried to infinity, the marvelous function of the Changes is made complete. Now, with nine transformations three lines are completed, and the inner trigram is established; if from this one extends the process infinitely so as to determine good and ill fortune, how could all possible undertakings under heaven not be fulfilled herein? Moreover, in the method of sorting yarrow stalks to seek a hexagram, four operations complete a change, and three transformations complete a line. Now, proceeding from three transformations to nine transformations, and from one line to three lines, the trigrams Qian 乾, Dui 兌, Li 离, and Zhen 震 are established, …

title: 成化十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
巽坎艮坤之體備矣然三畫之所成者內卦之貞而
已而外卦之悔未有也九變之所得者八卦之畫而
已而六十四卦未備也故曰八卦而小成夫三畫既
立由是再營九變而又得三畫則是引其端而伸之
由內卦而得外卦由三畫而得六畫斯大成矣六爻
既成然後視其爻之變與不變以為動靜則是觸其
類而長之一卦可變為六十四卦而六十四卦可變
為四千九十六卦於是定其占以示人吉未萌也使
人趨之無疑凶未見也使人避之無患于以開物而
===
成務于以通志而定業易之能事於是乎備故曰天
下之能事畢矣吁妙卦變於無窮極天下之能事易
之用其大矣乎抑考大傳此章首論天地之數次論
蓍策之數此論卦畫之數上文有曰四營而成易十
有八變而成卦盖言揲蓍求卦之法于以總一章之
事此言引伸觸類則占象推演之法下文所謂酬酢
佑神則又蓍卦之用而易之能事備矣吁旨哉

巽、坎、艮、坤之體備矣。然三畫之所成者，內卦之貞而已，而外卦之悔未有也；九變之所得者，八卦之畫而已，而六十四卦未備也。故曰「八卦而小成」。夫三畫既立，由是再營九變而又得三畫，則是引其端而伸之，由內卦而得外卦，由三畫而得六畫，斯大成矣。六爻既成，然後視其爻之變與不變以為動靜，則是觸其類而長之，一卦可變為六十四卦，而六十四卦可變為四千九十六卦。於是定其占以示人：吉未萌也，使人趨之無疑；凶未見也，使人避之無患。于以開物而成務，于以通志而定業，《易》之能事於是乎備。故曰「天下之能事畢矣」。吁！妙卦變於無窮，極天下之能事，《易》之用其大矣乎！抑考《大傳》此章，首論天地之數，次論蓍策之數，此論卦畫之數。上文有曰「四營而成易，十有八變而成卦」，盖言揲蓍求卦之法，于以總一章之事；此言「引伸觸類」，則占象推演之法；下文所謂「酬酢」、「佑神」，則又蓍卦之用，而《易》之能事備矣。吁，旨哉！

《書》
「明于五刑，以弼五教，期于予治，刑期于無刑。」
translation_en:
…and the forms of Xun, Kan, Gen, and Kun are complete. Yet what is formed by three lines is merely the lower trigram (zhen), while the upper trigram (hui) does not yet exist; what is obtained by nine transformations is merely the lines of the eight trigrams, while the sixty-four hexagrams are not yet complete. Therefore it says, "With the eight trigrams, there is the lesser completion." Once the three lines are established, from this one performs another nine transformations and obtains three more lines. This is drawing out its beginning and extending it: from the inner trigram one obtains the outer trigram, and from three lines one obtains six lines, which is the great completion. Once the six lines are formed, one then observes whether the lines change or do not change in order to determine movement and stillness. This is touching upon its category and expanding it: one hexagram can transform into sixty-four hexagrams, and the sixty-four hexagrams can transform into four thousand and ninety-six hexagrams. Thereupon, their prognostications are fixed to show to people: before good fortune has sprouted, it enables people to pursue it without doubt; before misfortune has appeared, it enables people to avoid it without harm. Thereby opening up knowledge of things and accomplishing tasks, and thereby communicating wills and settling enterprises, the capabilities of the Book of Changes (Yi) are thus complete. Therefore it says, "All possible undertakings under heaven are completed." Ah! Marvelous are the transformations of the hexagrams into infinity, exhausting all possible undertakings under heaven—how great is the application of the Changes! Moreover, if we examine this chapter of the Great Commentary (Dazhuan), it first discusses the numbers of heaven and earth, next discusses the numbers of the yarrow stalks, and here discusses the numbers of the hexagram lines. Above, it says, "Four operations complete a change, and eighteen transformations complete a hexagram," which speaks of the method of sorting yarrow stalks to seek a hexagram, thereby summarizing the matter of the whole chapter. Here, speaking of "drawing out and extending, touching upon categories," is the method of deducing prognostications and images. What the text below calls "responding to" and "assisting the spirit-like" is furthermore the function of the yarrow stalks and hexagrams, whereby the capabilities of the Changes are complete. Ah, how profound!

Book of Documents (Shu)
"Be intelligent in the use of the five punishments, so as to assist the five teachings, aiming at my rightful governance, and using punishment in the hope that there may be no punishments."

text:

大臣盡職以期夫人君之治而實期至於刑措之美

豈非實所以期至於無刑之地哉昔帝舜推用刑之

范諝

同考試官教諭毛批：作此題者，多於「期于予治，刑期無刑」處泛講不切，詞簡勁而意融貫者，僅見此篇。非究心本領之學者不能到，是宜錄出為學者矜式。

同考試官教授林批：本房作此題者，多不能體認章旨，不浮泛則拘束，讀之令人悶悶。惟此篇發出舜美皐陶之意，辭理俱到，奏黃鍾於瓦缶之餘，自不能不為之躍然。

考試官修撰鄭批：發明「刑期無刑」處甚佳。

考試官左諭德謝批：舜美皐陶明刑之功，篇中發明盡矣。

大臣盡職以期夫人君之治，而實期至於刑措之美。蓋刑者，輔治之法也；大臣明刑弼教以期人君之治，豈非實所以期至於無刑之地哉？昔帝舜推用刑之功以美皐陶，若曰：五刑有輕重也，爾皐陶能明其輕重之等以輔五品之教，期予從欲以治，使天下之為父子、君臣者，皆蔚然於綱常倫理之天，而所謂百姓
translation_en:
Fan Xu 范諝

Associate Examiner and County Director of Studies Mao's comment: Those writing on this topic mostly discuss the passage "looking forward to my orderly rule, using punishment in the hope that there will be no punishments" in a vague and imprecise manner. Only in this essay do we see diction that is concise and forceful while the meaning is thoroughly integrated. None but a scholar who has devoted his mind to fundamental principles could attain this; it ought to be transcribed and published as a model for scholars.

Associate Examiner and Prefectural Director of Studies Lin's comment: In my examination ward, those writing on this topic were mostly unable to grasp the import of the passage; if they were not superficial and vague, they were overly cramped, making the reader feel stifled and bored. Only this essay brings out the meaning of Shun's praise of Gao Yao, achieving perfection in both expression and principle. Like striking the Yellow Bell pitch-pipe after hearing clay pots, one cannot help but leap with joy at it.

Examiner and Senior Compiler Zheng's comment: The elucidation of the passage "using punishment in the hope that there will be no punishments" is excellent.

Examiner and Left Admonisher Xie's comment: Shun's praise of Gao Yao's merit in clarifying punishments is fully elucidated in this essay.

When a great minister fulfills his duty in looking forward to his ruler's orderly governance, what he truly hopes to achieve is the perfection of setting punishments aside altogether. For punishments are a method to assist in governance; when a great minister clarifies punishments to assist moral instruction in expectation of the ruler's orderly governance, is this not truly how he hopes to reach a state where there are no punishments? In antiquity, Emperor Shun attributed the merit of applying punishments to praise Gao Yao, as if to say: The five punishments have degrees of severity. You, Gao Yao, are able to clarify the gradations of their severity to assist the instruction of the five human relationships, looking forward to my achieving governance in accordance with my wishes, causing all fathers and sons, rulers and ministers under heaven to flourish within the natural sphere of the cardinal guides and moral relationships, so that what is called the hundred surnames…

title: 成化十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
不親者無有焉五刑有取舍也汝皐陶能明其取舍
之用以弼五常之教期予德洽民心使天下之為夫
婦長幼朋友者皆怡然於民彜物則之域而所謂五
品不遜者無有焉是始之父子不親君臣不義固不
免用刑以一之矣然爾之心非淫刑以逞也惟欲期
父子親君臣義使刑雖具而無所用焉耳始之夫婦
不别長幼不叙朋友不信固不免用法以齊之矣然
爾之心非倚法以削也實欲期夫婦别長幼叙朋友
信使法徒設而無所施焉耳皐陶明刑之功如此帝
===
舜安得不稱美之歟抑考此章帝舜既以刑措之美
歸之皐陶明刑之功下文皐陶不敢以為己功而歸
之帝舜好生之德噫君不自以為功而歸之臣臣不
敢以為功而歸之君君臣交致其美明良相逢千載
而下猶可想見一時氣象
皇天既付中國民越厥疆土于先王肆王惟德
用和懌先後迷民用懌先王受命已若茲監
惟曰欲至于萬年惟王子子孫孫永保民
陳賓

而下猶可想見一時氣象

用和懌先後迷民用懌先王受命已若茲監

punctuated:
不親者，無有焉。五刑有取舍也，汝皐陶能明其取舍之用，以弼五常之教，期予德洽民心，使天下之為夫婦、長幼、朋友者，皆怡然於民彜物則之域，而所謂五品不遜者，無有焉。是始之父子不親、君臣不義，固不免用刑以一之矣；然爾之心非淫刑以逞也，惟欲期父子親、君臣義，使刑雖具而無所用焉耳。始之夫婦不别、長幼不叙、朋友不信，固不免用法以齊之矣；然爾之心非倚法以削也，實欲期夫婦别、長幼叙、朋友信，使法徒設而無所施焉耳。」皐陶明刑之功如此，帝舜安得不稱美之歟？抑考此章，帝舜既以刑措之美歸之皐陶明刑之功，下文皐陶不敢以為己功，而歸之帝舜好生之德。噫！君不自以為功而歸之臣，臣不敢以為功而歸之君，君臣交致其美，明良相逢，千載而下，猶可想見一時氣象。

皇天既付中國民越厥疆土于先王，肆王惟德用，和懌先後迷民，用懌先王受命。已！若茲監，惟曰欲至于萬年，惟王子子孫孫永保民。

陳賓
translation_en:
… not being affectionate toward one another no longer exists. The Five Punishments involve choices of when to apply or withhold them; you, Gao Yao, are able to clarify the application of such choices so as to assist the instruction of the Five Constant Virtues, hoping that my virtue will permeate the hearts of the people, causing all in the realm who are husband and wife, old and young, or friends to dwell harmoniously within the bounds of human moral norms and the principles of things, so that what is called the Five Relationships being uncompliant no longer exists. Thus, when at first fathers and sons were not affectionate and rulers and ministers were not righteous, it was indeed unavoidable to use punishments to unify them; yet your intention was not to indulge in excessive punishments to gratify yourself, but solely to hope that fathers and sons would be affectionate and rulers and ministers righteous, so that although punishments are prepared, there is no occasion to use them. When at first husbands and wives had no proper distinction, old and young had no proper order, and friends were not trustworthy, it was indeed unavoidable to use the law to regulate them; yet your intention was not to rely on the law to be harsh and exacting, but truly to hope that husbands and wives would have proper distinction, old and young would have proper order, and friends would be trustworthy, so that the laws are merely set up and there is no place to enforce them." Since Gao Yao's merit in clarifying punishments was like this, how could Emperor Shun not praise and extol him? Moreover, examining this passage, after Emperor Shun attributed the excellence of setting aside punishments to Gao Yao's merit in clarifying punishments, in the following text Gao Yao did not dare to claim it as his own merit, and instead attributed it to Emperor Shun's virtue of loving life. Ah! The ruler did not claim the merit for himself but attributed it to his minister, and the minister did not dare to claim it as his merit but attributed it to his ruler. Ruler and minister mutually accorded praise to one another—an enlightened sovereign and a worthy minister meeting together. Even a thousand years later, one can still imagine the spirit of that age.

"August Heaven has already entrusted the people of the Central States and their territory to the former kings. Now may the King employ only virtue to harmonize and gladden, and guide and care for the misguided people, thereby gladdening the mandate received by the former kings. Indeed! Looking upon this as a mirror, we say only that we wish to reach ten thousand years, and that the King's sons and grandsons may forever preserve the people."

Chen Bin 陳賓

title: 成化十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭毛批此題頗長作者多分割失
旨而詞又冗泛令人厭觀惟此篇形容有周大臣
告君之意無遺且詞氣動盪發越讀之如親見當
時真傑作也宜錄以冠本房
同考試官教授林批說出周家臣下責難祈祝
君上之意忠誠懇切宛然當時氣象讀之令人一
唱三嘆
考試官修撰鄭批周家大臣忠愛之心藹然
言表
===
考試官左諭德謝批理明詞贍可取
大臣告君既言天眷前王而勉以繼述之責復欲監
已所陳而祈以天命之永盖上天重其託於先王後
王當明德化民以盡繼述之責也苟不能監大臣之
所陳戒則亦何以保天命於有永哉昔有周大臣進
戒其君之意若曰中國人民吾不知其幾千萬姓也
今焉一民莫非先王之臣者孰畀之哉天監厥德而
畀之也中國疆土吾不知其幾千萬里也今焉尺地
莫非先王所有者孰與之哉天監厥德而與之也然

punctuated:
同考試官教諭毛批：此題頗長，作者多分割失旨，而詞又冗泛，令人厭觀。惟此篇形容有周大臣告君之意無遺，且詞氣動盪發越，讀之如親見當時，真傑作也，宜錄以冠本房。

考試官修撰鄭批：周家大臣忠愛之心，藹然言表。
考試官左諭德謝批：理明詞贍，可取。
大臣告君，既言天眷前王，而勉以繼述之責；復欲監已所陳，而祈以天命之永。盖上天重其託於先王，後王當明德化民，以盡繼述之責也。苟不能監大臣之所陳戒，則亦何以保天命於有永哉？昔有周大臣進戒其君之意，若曰：「中國人民，吾不知其幾千萬姓也。今焉一民莫非先王之臣者，孰畀之哉？天監厥德而畀之也。中國疆土，吾不知其幾千萬里也。今焉尺地莫非先王所有者，孰與之哉？天監厥德而與之也。然
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Mao: This topic is rather long, and most writers dissect it to the point of losing its main purport, while their phrasing is prolix and diffuse, making them tiresome to read. Only this essay exhaustively captures the spirit in which the great minister of Zhou addressed his ruler. Moreover, its tone and vigor surge and soar; reading it is like witnessing that era in person. It is truly a masterpiece and ought to be recorded at the head of my ward.

Comment by Associate Examiner and Professor Lin: It brings out the intentions of the Zhou minister in holding his sovereign to high standards and praying for his blessing. Loyal, sincere, and earnest, it vividly evokes the atmosphere of the time; reading it makes one chant a line and sigh thrice in admiration.

Comment by Examiner and Senior Compiler Zheng: The loyal and affectionate heart of the great minister of Zhou shines gently beyond the words.

Comment by Examiner and Left Admonisher Xie: The reasoning is clear and the diction rich; it is worthy of selection.

In addressing his ruler, the great minister first speaks of Heaven's favor toward the former kings and exhorts him with the responsibility of carrying on their legacy; he then wishes the ruler to heed what he has set forth and prays for the perpetuity of Heaven's Mandate. For High Heaven placed a weighty trust in the former kings, and the successor king ought to manifest bright virtue to transform the people, thereby fulfilling his responsibility of continuing their work. If he cannot heed the admonitions set forth by his great minister, how then can he preserve Heaven's Mandate forever? In antiquity, the meaning of the admonition presented by the great minister of Zhou to his ruler was as if to say: "As for the people of the Central States, I do not know how many tens of millions of surnames they number. Now, that there is not a single person who is not a subject of the former kings—who bestowed them? Heaven beheld their virtue and bestowed them. As for the territory of the Central States, I do not know how many tens of millions of li it spans. Now, that there is not a foot of land that does not belong to the former kings—who granted it? Heaven beheld their virtue and granted it. Yet…"

title: 成化十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
上天付託固在於先王而先王付託則在於後王是
故迷惑之民先王盖嘗化之有未徧今王必明德以
和悅之使皆歸于德化之中以慰其受命之心可也
染惡之民先王盖嘗新之有未周今王必以德而勞
来之使咸囿於倫理之內以悅其受命之心可也大
臣既以此而勉其君於是復告之以為我所陳明德
得天之說誠致治之格言王當監之而不可忘也我
所陳用德化民之訓乃保邦之要道王當視之而不
可忽也然我進告之言雖有盡而祈祝之意則無窮
===
盖欲祈之以貴吾王貴為天子不待吾之祈矣惟願
綿曆數於萬有千歲而王之子孫是繼是承者皆有
以永厎烝民之生焉欲祈之以富吾王富有四海不
待吾之祈矣惟願享國祚於億萬斯年而王之子孫
以嗣以續者咸有以永康四海之民焉噫大臣以是
而責難祈祝於君其忠愛之心為何如哉抑斯言也
乃有周大臣之告君者而簡編錯於梓材篇末觀其
進戒之詞誠切懇至祈祝之意忠愛無窮求之當時
非篤棐周召其孰能與于斯

上天付託固在於先王而先王付託則在於後王是
故迷惑之民先王蓋嘗化之有未偏今王必明德以
和悅之使皆歸于德化之中以慰其受命之心可也
染惡之民先王蓋嘗新之有未周今王必以德而勞
來之使咸囿於倫理之内以悅其受命之心可也大
臣既以此而勉其君於是復告之以為我所陳明德
得天之說誠致治之格言王當監之而不可忘也我
所陳用德化民之訓乃保邦之要道王當視之而不
可忽也然我進告之言雖有盡而祈祝之意則無窮
===

綿曆數於萬有千歲而王之子孫是繼是承者皆有

待吾之祈矣惟願享國祚於億萬斯年而王之子孫
以嗣以續者咸有以永康四海之民焉噫大臣以是
而責難祈祝於君其忠愛之心為何如哉抑斯言也
乃有周大臣之告君者而簡編錯於梓材篇末觀其
進戒之詞誠切懇至祈祝之意忠愛無窮求之當時
非篤棐周召其孰能與于斯
punctuated: 上天付託固在於先王，而先王付託則在於後王。是故迷惑之民，先王盖嘗化之有未徧，今王必明德以和悅之，使皆歸于德化之中，以慰其受命之心可也；染惡之民，先王盖嘗新之有未周，今王必以德而勞来之，使咸囿於倫理之內，以悅其受命之心可也。大臣既以此而勉其君，於是復告之，以為我所陳明德得天之說，誠致治之格言，王當監之而不可忘也；我所陳用德化民之訓，乃保邦之要道，王當視之而不可忽也。然我進告之言雖有盡，而祈祝之意則無窮。盖欲祈之以貴，吾王貴為天子，不待吾之祈矣，惟願綿曆數於萬有千歲，而王之子孫是繼是承者，皆有以永厎烝民之生焉；欲祈之以富，吾王富有四海，不待吾之祈矣，惟願享國祚於億萬斯年，而王之子孫以嗣以續者，咸有以永康四海之民焉。噫！大臣以是而責難祈祝於君，其忠愛之心為何如哉！抑斯言也，乃有周大臣之告君者，而簡編錯於《梓材》篇末。觀其進戒之詞，誠切懇至，祈祝之意，忠愛無窮，求之當時，非篤棐周、召，其孰能與于斯？
translation_en:
…While High Heaven's trust was indeed placed in the former kings, the former kings' trust is placed in the succeeding king. Therefore, as for the deluded people whom the former kings transformed but not yet universally, the present king must make bright his virtue to harmonize and please them, causing them all to return within the fold of moral transformation, so as to comfort the hearts of the former kings who received the Mandate. As for the people tainted by evil whom the former kings renewed but not yet completely, the present king must use virtue to encourage and draw them in, causing them all to be encompassed within moral human relationships, so as to gladden the hearts of the former kings who received the Mandate. Having thus exhorted his ruler, the great minister then further addressed him, saying: "What I have set forth concerning the doctrine of making bright one's virtue to win Heaven's favor is truly a maxim for achieving good governance; Your Majesty ought to take it as a mirror and never forget it. What I have set forth concerning the instruction of using virtue to transform the people is the essential Way for preserving the state; Your Majesty ought to regard it and never neglect it. Yet although the words of my admonition have an end, the intent of my prayers and blessings is boundless. Should I wish to pray for your nobility, my King is already noble as the Son of Heaven and needs not my prayer; I only wish that the dynastic calendar may be prolonged for tens of thousands of years, and that the King's descendants who succeed and inherit from him may all forever secure the livelihood of the multitude of the people. Should I wish to pray for your wealth, my King already possesses the riches of the Four Seas and needs not my prayer; I only wish that the throne may be enjoyed for hundreds of millions of years, and that the King's descendants who carry on the line may all forever bring peace and well-being to the people of the Four Seas."

Alas! When a great minister thus urges difficult achievements upon his ruler and offers prayers for him, how profound is his heart of loyalty and affection! Moreover, these words were spoken by a great minister of the Zhou to his ruler, though the bamboo slips were mistakenly placed at the end of the "Catalpa Timber" (Zicai) chapter [of the Book of Documents]. When we examine the words of his admonition, so sincere, earnest, and thorough, and the intent of his prayers, so endlessly loyal and affectionate—if we seek their author in that age, who else could have been capable of this if not the devotedly assisting Dukes of Zhou and Shao?

title: 成化十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
詩
四鍭如樹序賓以不侮曾孫維主酒醴維醹酌
以大斗以祈黃耇黃耇台背
徐寬
同考試官教諭原批本房詩經九百餘卷而佳
作甚少此卷七篇皆平整而此篇尤純雅可錄佳
作也置之高選孰曰不宜
同考試官學正胡批題本平易作者非泛則畧
不愜人意晚得此篇明白純正有周王者篤親親
===
之意宛然可見
考試官修撰鄭批遣辭溫潤善說詩者也
考試官左諭德謝批詞氣春容得溫柔敦厚之體
王者之燕所親也射於終而尚乎德飲於終而祝乎
壽夫親親之恩不可不厚也今王者之燕親射飲雖
終而猶論德祝壽之無已其親厚之意不其至歟是
詩為祭畢而燕父兄耆老而作也謂夫侍御獻酬既
有節矣飲食歌樂亦盡禮矣而賓主之情尚未洽也
可不較藝以為樂乎斯時也四鍭徧釋而皆中乎鵠

王者之燕所親也，射於終而尚乎德，飲於終而祝乎壽。夫親親之恩，不可不厚也。今王者之燕親，射、飲雖終，而猶論德祝壽之無已，其親厚之意，不其至歟？是詩為祭畢而燕父兄耆老而作也，謂夫侍御獻酬既有節矣，飲食歌樂亦盡禮矣，而賓主之情尚未洽也，可不較藝以為樂乎？斯時也，四鍭徧釋而皆中乎鵠，
translation_en:
Classic of Poetry (Shijing)

"The four metal-tipped arrows are as if planted; the guests are ranked according to their lack of insolence. The distant descendant is the host; the spirits and sweet wine are rich; he pours them with a large ladle, to pray for yellow-haired elders—yellow-haired elders with globe-fish backs." [Ode "Xingwei" 行葦]

Xu Kuan 徐寬

Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Yuan: In my ward there were over nine hundred papers on the Classic of Poetry, yet very few fine works. All seven essays in this paper are balanced and well-regulated, and this piece is especially pure and elegant—a fine work worthy of selection. Placing it high among the chosen, who would say it is inappropriate?

Comment by Associate Examiner and Subprefectural Director of Studies Hu: The topic is inherently plain and easy, so writers were either vague or sketchy, failing to satisfy expectations. Late in the reading I came upon this piece, which is clear and pure; the Zhou kings' earnest affection for their kin can be vividly seen in it.

Comment by Examiner and Senior Compiler Zheng: The phrasing is warm and lustrous; he is one who knows well how to expound the Poetry.

Comment by Examiner and Left Admonisher Xie: The diction and vital breath are unhurried and expansive, attaining the gentle, kindly, and sincere style proper to the Poetry.

When the true king feasts his kinsmen, at the conclusion of the archery he esteems virtue, and at the conclusion of the drinking he prays for longevity. Now, the grace of affection toward kinsmen cannot but be generous. Here, in the true king's feasting of his kinsmen, even though the archery and drinking are drawing to a close, he still endlessly weighs their virtue and prays for their longevity—is not his affectionate and generous intent at its utmost? This ode was composed for the feast given to paternal uncles, elder brothers, and aged elders after a sacrifice is completed. It says that after the attendants' offering and exchanging of toasts have been conducted with due measure, and the food, drink, singing, and music have exhausted the rites, the feelings between guests and host are still not completely harmonized—how could they not compete in the art of archery to make merry? At this time, the four metal-tipped arrows are all loosed and every one hits the target…

title: 成化十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
如手就樹堅而不敧也四矢既均而皆貫乎革如手
就樹正而不偏也省括于度藝固精矣猶必無憮無
傲不以己之中而驕者為可尚焉發彼有的射固善
矣猶必無偕立無踰言不以人之不中而傲者為可
貴焉非射於終而尚德乎夫既射以為樂矣而燕猶
未終也曾孫為主復登筵焉可不酌酒以為頌乎斯
時也獻爵尚多則旨酒思柔而汁滓維厚也舉觶無
筭則大斗是酌而器用如式也然飲此旨酒豈為口
腹之飲而已乎以頤養天和頭髪白復黄面如凍梨
===
而獲壽之徵焉酌此大斗豈為飲食之具而已乎以
保養天倪願黄耇既介背有台文而得壽之兆焉又
非飲於終而祝壽乎吁射雖終而禮猶飭飲將終而
祝益隆王者之於父兄耆老何其情有加而意無窮
也歟抑王者之燕親親既曰以祈黄耇黄耇台背又
曰以引以翼以介景福是不徒有福而有德以享其
壽也及既醉之答君既曰君子萬年介爾景福又曰
高朗令終令終有俶是不徒有其始而又有以善其
終也上以是施之下以是報之忠厚之意溢於言表
