以定其罪。必情罪相應，而後罰加焉。其不然者，正以故出故入之條，律以受囑枉法之罪，刑其濫乎？草茅有懷，思欲獻之吾君吾相而無由。執事先生倘有取於負暄之愚，上裨廟謨之萬一，亦豈非仁人君子之心哉！

第四問
有儒者之學術，必有儒者之事功。儒者之道，其大矣哉！詩、書、禮、樂，其業也；仁、義、禮、智，其蘊也；齊家、治國、平天下，其用也。以之為上則為德，以之為下則為民，以之為天下則無所不宜，而況於為吏乎？況於為將乎？自儒學不明，俎豆、軍旅分為二途，俗吏、迂儒互相攻呵。將之鄙儒，則曰「措大」；吏之鄙儒，則曰「迂腐」。噫！儒道果若是小耶？儒道與天地竝，而不行則非一日矣。彼子游學道愛人，而絃歌以化武城；子賤尊賢取友，而彈琴以治單父。儒者之效，亦畧見於吏已。若文翁治蜀郡而首興學校，兒寬以經術而潤飾吏事，劉昆之仁及猛虎，韓愈之信孚鱷魚，則儒者之粗跡，而韓愈道濟天下之溺，其優者歟？
translation_en:
…in order to determine the offense. Only when the circumstances and the charge correspond should punishment be imposed. For those who fail to do so, if they are rectified by the statutes against deliberate exoneration or deliberate incrimination, and judged by the crime of perverting the law at another's behest, will punishments ever be abused? Living in rustic obscurity, I cherish these thoughts and wish to present them to our Sovereign and our Ministers, yet had no way to do so. Should you, the venerable Examiners, find something worth adopting in the humble offering of a rustic warming himself in the sun, so as to contribute even one part in ten thousand to the counsels of the imperial court, would this not also fulfill the heart of a humane man and a gentleman?

Fourth Question:
Where there is the learning of a Confucian scholar, there must be the practical achievements of a Confucian scholar. Great indeed is the Way of the Confucian! The Odes, the Documents, the Rites, and Music are its studies; humaneness, righteousness, propriety, and wisdom are its inner substance; regulating the family, governing the state, and bringing peace to the world are its applications. Employed from above, it becomes virtue; employed from below, it serves the people; employed throughout the world, there is nowhere it is not fitting—and how much more so in serving as an administrative official? How much more so in serving as a general? Ever since Confucian learning ceased to be clearly understood, ritual vessels and military affairs have split into two separate paths, while vulgar officials and pedantic scholars attack and berate one another. When generals disdain Confucians, they call them "pedants" (cuoda); when administrative officials disdain Confucians, they call them "impractical" (yufu). Alas! Is the Confucian Way really so petty as this? The Confucian Way stands coequal with Heaven and Earth, yet it has failed to be put into practice for more than a single day. Consider how Ziyou (Yan Yan 言偃) studied the Way and loved the people, transforming Wucheng through stringed instruments and song; or how Zijian (Fu Buqi 宓不齊) honored the worthy and made friends of the virtuous, governing Shanfu while playing the zither. The efficacy of the Confucian was thus already roughly seen in civil administration. As for Wen Weng 文翁 governing Shu Commandery and first establishing schools, Ni Kuan 兒寬 adorning administrative affairs with classical scholarship, Liu Kun 劉昆 whose humaneness reached even fierce tigers, and Han Yu 韓愈 whose good faith moved even crocodiles—these were but the rough outward traces of Confucians, whereas Han Yu's rescuing the drowning world through the Way was perhaps the finest among them…

title: 成化十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
跡而韓愈道濟天下之溺其優者歟文武吉甫
而著北伐之功詩書郤縠而成伯晉之績儒者
之效亦畧見於將已若祭遵之雅歌投壺而漢
祚中興羊祜之輕裘緩帶而吳人自懷孔明表
出師而敵畏如虎杜預註春秋而敵破如竹又
儒者之緒餘而孔明有儒者氣象其尤者歟彼
公孫弘之曲學以湯旱歸之桀張禹之奸佞謂
聖人不語怪此儒吏之罪人也陸機嘲弄文賦
而大敗河橋房琯好談釋老而喪師陳濤此又
===
儒將之罪人也其所守何道所讀何書而奸欺
僨事如此尚可謂之儒乎宜為武夫俗吏小之
也噫儒之道豈易言哉通天地人之謂儒必達
而為堯為舜窮而為孔為孟斯無負於儒矣方
今文教誕興群才效用而執事尚嘆夫功利之徒
不能無文武之才猶未見然則如之何而後可
愚請於士也慎科貢之選先德行而後文藝重
考課之法先教化而後政刑如是則吏皆儒矣
於將也設武舉以羅韜畧之士而世閥不論也

translation_en: …traces, while Han Yu 韓愈, whose Way rescued the world from drowning, was the superior one among them! Yin Jifu 尹吉甫, both civil and martial, achieved the merit of the northern expedition; Xi Hu 郤縠, versed in the Odes and Documents (Shi shu), accomplished the feat of making Jin the hegemon. Thus the efficacy of Confucians has also been roughly seen in generals. As for Zhai Zun 祭遵 singing refined songs and playing pitch-pot while the Han fortune was restored; Yang Hu 羊祜 wearing light furs and a loose girdle while the people of Wu naturally cherished him; Kongming 孔明 [Zhuge Liang 諸葛亮] submitting the Memorial on Sending Forth the Army (Chushi biao) while the enemy feared him like a tiger; and Du Yu 杜預 writing commentaries on the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) while splitting the enemy like bamboo—these again were the residual accomplishments of Confucians, and Kongming, who possessed the bearing of a Confucian, was the most outstanding among them! As for that Gongsun Hong 公孫弘 with his crooked learning, who attributed the drought of Tang 湯 to Jie 桀; and Zhang Yu 張禹 with his treacherous flattery, who claimed that the Sage did not speak of prodigies—these were criminals among Confucian officials. Lu Ji 陸機, who toyed with literary compositions and suffered a great defeat at Heqiao; and Fang Guan 房琯, who loved to talk of Buddhism and Daoism and lost his army at Chentao—these again were criminals among Confucian generals. What Way did they uphold, and what books did they read, that they were so deceitful and ruined affairs like this? Can they still be called Confucians? It is fitting that martial men and vulgar clerks belittle them! Alas, how can the Way of the Confucian be easily spoken of? One who comprehends heaven, earth, and man is called a Confucian; only when one attains prominence and becomes like Yao 堯 and Shun 舜, or remains in obscurity and becomes like Confucius (Kong 孔) and Mencius (Meng 孟), does one not fail the name of Confucian. Right now, civil education broadly flourishes and a multitude of talents render service, yet Your Excellency still laments that followers of功利 (utility and profit) cannot be eliminated and talents both civil and martial are still not seen. If so, what then should be done so that all will be well? I humbly propose that with regard to scholars, we be careful in selection through examinations and tribute, putting moral conduct first and literary art second; and give weight to the methods of performance evaluation, putting moral transformation first and governance and punishment second—if we do this, then all officials will be Confucians. With regard to generals, we should establish military examinations to net men versed in strategy and tactics, regardless of hereditary status;…

title: 成化十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
嚴推選以求文武之將而行伍不計也如是則
將皆儒矣殆見在廷也則一夔一契有文章焉
有政事焉在邊也則一韓一范有文事焉有武
備焉亦莫非吾儒分內事而儒者之效又豈不
暴於天下哉謹以是為執事復
第五問
論天下之事者固當達古之制尤必酌今之宜
泥於今而不達於古俗吏之見也滯於古而不
通乎今迂儒之論也徐庶有言識時務者在俊
===
傑愚非俊傑也何足以當執事之問然亦安敢
自棄於明教之外乎夫周人之鄉舉里選也有
閭師焉以書其德有族師焉以月其能論定然
後官之任官然後爵之固未嘗限其數也自隋
唐以科舉取士而此意泯矣故前輩嘗有欲廢
之者而愚以為不可廢且不必廢也惟當於科
舉之中寓里選之法鄉考其德而後升之學學
考其才而後升之有司主司又察言以觀其行
因文以考其心期必得乎名實相須之士使有

論天下之事者，固當達古之制，尤必酌今之宜。泥於今而不達於古，俗吏之見也；滯於古而不通乎今，迂儒之論也。徐庶有言：「識時務者在俊傑。」愚非俊傑也，何足以當執事之問？然亦安敢自棄於明教之外乎？夫周人之鄉舉里選也，有閭師焉以書其德，有族師焉以月其能，論定然後官之，任官然後爵之，固未嘗限其數也。自隋唐以科舉取士，而此意泯矣。故前輩嘗有欲廢之者，而愚以為不可廢，且不必廢也。惟當於科舉之中，寓里選之法：鄉考其德而後升之學，學考其才而後升之有司；主司又察言以觀其行，因文以考其心，期必得乎名實相須之士，使有
translation_en:
…make recommendations and selections strict in order to seek generals endowed with both civil and military competence, without regard to whether they rose from the ranks. If this is done, then all generals will be Confucians. We shall soon see that at court, every one will be a Kui 夔 or a Xie 契, possessing both literary learning and administrative skill; and on the frontiers, every one will be a Han Qi 韓琦 or a Fan Zhongyan 范仲淹, possessing both civil culture and military preparedness. None of these is outside the proper duty of us Confucians, and how could the efficacy of Confucians not be made manifest throughout the empire? I respectfully offer this in reply to Your Excellency.

Question Five

Those who discuss the affairs of the empire must of course understand the institutions of antiquity, yet they must especially weigh what is suitable for the present. To be bogged down in the present without understanding antiquity is the view of a vulgar clerk; to be mired in antiquity without comprehending the present is the discourse of a pedantic Confucian. Xu Shu 徐庶 once said: "Those who understand the exigencies of the times are outstanding heroes." Ignorant as I am, I am no outstanding hero—how could I be worthy of answering Your Excellency's question? Yet how dare I cast myself outside your enlightened instruction?

In the system of recommendation from districts and selection from villages practiced by the men of Zhou, there were Neighborhood Heads (lüshi 閭師) to record people's moral conduct and Clan Heads (zushi 族師) to make monthly assessments of their abilities. Only after evaluation of a man was settled was he given office, and only after he had served in office was he granted rank and emolument; indeed, they never set a quota on their numbers. Since the Sui and Tang dynasties began selecting scholars through the civil service examinations, this original intent has vanished. Consequently, predecessors at times wished to abolish the examinations, yet I humbly believe that they cannot be abolished, and moreover need not be abolished. We ought simply to embed the method of village selection within the examination system: let the local community examine a man's moral conduct before promoting him to the school, and let the school examine his talent before promoting him to the authorities; then let the examiners scrutinize his words to observe his conduct, and examine his mind through his writing, hoping without fail to obtain scholars whose reputation and reality correspond, so that those who possess…

title: 成化十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
學者不至遺棄無學者不至倖進則觧額之拘
正所以嚴去取又何必廢之以啓任情濫取之
弊哉三代之建官也兎罝為公侯之仇鷹揚居
尚父之任爵罔及惡德惟其賢官不及私昵惟
其能固未嘗論其年資也自裴光庭以資格銓
選而此制泯矣故先正嘗有欲去之者而愚以
為不必去且不可去也惟當於年資之中兼考
課之法審其事之難易別其人之賢愚方其選
也才者常於其難不才者常於其易及其擢也
===
難者常速而易者常緩間又簡拔茂才異等之
人使有才者知所勸不才者知所警則雖年資
之論亦足以定人心又何必去之以開奔競躁
進之途乎飢民之患極矣計將安施古人三年
耕必餘一年之積九年耕必餘三年之積其法
不可復矣而欲都邑之粟自足賑恤其民莫若
倣李悝平糴之法豐年增價以糴凶年減價以
糶小飢則發小熟之所藏中飢則發中熟之所
藏大飢則發大熟之所藏而又謹其出納無為

學者不至遺棄，無學者不至倖進，則觧額之拘，正所以嚴去取，又何必廢之，以啓任情濫取之弊哉？
三代之建官也，兎罝為公侯之仇，鷹揚居尚父之任，爵罔及惡德，惟其賢；官不及私昵，惟其能，固未嘗論其年資也。自裴光庭以資格銓選，而此制泯矣。故先正嘗有欲去之者，而愚以為不必去，且不可去也。惟當於年資之中，兼考課之法，審其事之難易，別其人之賢愚。方其選也，才者常於其難，不才者常於其易；及其擢也，難者常速，而易者常緩。間又簡拔茂才異等之人，使有才者知所勸，不才者知所警，則雖年資之論，亦足以定人心，又何必去之，以開奔競躁進之途乎？
飢民之患極矣，計將安施？古人三年耕必餘一年之積，九年耕必餘三年之積，其法不可復矣。而欲都邑之粟，自足賑恤其民，莫若倣李悝平糴之法：豐年增價以糴，凶年減價以糶；小飢則發小熟之所藏，中飢則發中熟之所藏，大飢則發大熟之所藏。而又謹其出納，無為
translation_en:
…true learning are not left abandoned, and those without learning do not advance through sheer luck. Thus, the restriction of the provincial examination quotas is precisely the means to make selection strict; why must we abolish it and thereby open the door to the abuse of arbitrary and indiscriminate selection?

In the establishment of offices during the Three Dynasties, a rabbit-netter became the companion of dukes and marquises, and the one who soared like a falcon occupied the post of Father Shang [Jiang Ziya]. Nobility was never conferred upon the wicked, but only upon the worthy; office was never given to private favorites, but only to the capable—they certainly neverreckoned by seniority and qualifications. Ever since Pei Guang庭裴光庭 instituted selection based on seniority and qualifications (zige), that ancient system has vanished. Therefore, worthies of the past once wished to do away with seniority rules, yet I believe they need not be discarded, and indeed cannot be discarded. We ought only to combine the method of performance evaluation within the system of seniority: examine the difficulty or ease of their duties, and distinguish the worthiness or foolishness of the men. At the time of their initial selection, the talented should regularly be assigned to difficult posts, and the untalented to easy ones; when it comes to their promotion, those in difficult posts should regularly be advanced quickly, while those in easy ones should regularly be advanced slowly. From time to time, we should also specially select men of flourishing talent and exceptional grade, so that the talented know what encourages them and the untalented know what warns them. Then, even with the consideration of seniority, it will suffice to settle men's minds; why must we discard it and thereby open the path to competitive scrambling and rash advancement?

The distress of starving people has reached an extreme; what plan is to be applied? Among the ancients, three years of plowing necessarily left a surplus of one year's store, and nine years of plowing necessarily left a surplus of three years' store, but that method can no longer be restored. If we wish the grain of the cities and towns to be self-sufficient for relieving their people, nothing is better than imitating Li Kui's 李悝 method of equitable grain purchase (pingdi): in years of abundance, increase the price to buy grain in; in years of dearth, reduce the price to sell grain out. In a minor famine, distribute what was stored from a minor harvest; in a medium famine, distribute what was stored from a medium harvest; and in a great famine, distribute what was stored from a great harvest. Furthermore, be careful with its disbursement and receipt, so that it is not…

title: 成化十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
吏胥之所竊時其收穫無為鳥鼠之所耗則荒
其有不備乎調兵之患久矣謀將安施古者戍
其地則乗其地之馬戰其野則食其野之粟其
制不可復矣而欲邊衛之兵自足保障一方莫
若倣蘇洵權書之策興屯田之利嚴斥堠之警
未戰養其財方戰養其力既戰養其氣而又四
時閱武無忘不虞推轂命將勿從中制則兵其
有不備乎雖然此四者又皆在得人而行之所
謂任法不如任人是也愚也一介草茅何敢言
===
天下之事然嫠緯之於周漆室之於魯亦情之
不能自已也惟執事亮其心而進之教之幸甚

天下之事然嫠緯之於周漆室之於魯亦情之

punctuated: 吏胥之所竊，時其收穫，無為鳥鼠之所耗，則荒其有不備乎？調兵之患久矣，謀將安施？古者戍其地則乗其地之馬，戰其野則食其野之粟。其制不可復矣，而欲邊衛之兵自足保障一方，莫若倣蘇洵《權書》之策：興屯田之利，嚴斥堠之警；未戰養其財，方戰養其力，既戰養其氣。而又四時閱武，無忘不虞，推轂命將，勿從中制，則兵其有不備乎？雖然，此四者，又皆在得人而行之，所謂「任法不如任人」是也。愚也一介草茅，何敢言天下之事？然嫠緯之於周，漆室之於魯，亦情之不能自已也。惟執事亮其心而進之教之，幸甚。
translation_en:
…stolen by clerks and subofficial functionaries, and time the storage properly so that it is not wasted by birds and rats—then how could famine relief fail to be prepared?

The affliction of transferring troops has lasted a long time; what plan should be applied? In antiquity, those who garrisoned a region rode the horses of that region, and those who fought in a territory ate the grain of that territory. That system cannot be restored, yet if we wish the troops of the frontier guards to be self-sufficient in defending their territory, nothing is better than to imitate the strategy in Su Xun’s 蘇洵 Book of Weighing (Quanshu): develop the benefits of military agricultural colonies (tuntian) and strictly maintain the vigilance of lookouts and beacons; before battle, nurture their resources; during battle, nurture their strength; and after battle, nurture their spirit. Moreover, review the troops in all four seasons so as not to forget unexpected dangers, and when pushing the wheel-hub to commission a general, do not control him from the court—then how could military defense fail to be prepared?

Even so, all four of these matters depend on obtaining the right men to carry them out; this is what is meant by the saying, "relying on laws is not as good as relying on men." Ignorant as I am, a mere rustic from the thatched huts, how dare I speak of the affairs of the realm? Yet like the widow worrying over her weaving in Zhou and the woman of Qishi 漆室 in Lu, it is simply a feeling I cannot restrain. May Your Excellency understand my heart, advance me, and instruct me—that would be my greatest fortune.

translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination

In the autumn of the tenth year of the Chenghua reign (1474), at the time of the great triennial examination, the Prefect of Yingtian Prefecture, His Majesty's servant Chongzhi 崇志, and the Vice Prefect, His Majesty's servant Ang 昂, petitioned to gather the scholars of the Directorate of Education and the Southern Metropolitan Area to examine them, in accordance with precedent. Thereupon, His Majesty issued a decree appointing his servants Yikui 一夔 [Xie Yikui 謝一夔] and Jing 璟 [Zhang Jing 張璟] as Examiners. Your servants reverently received the illustrious mandate, filled with awe morning and night, fearing only that we might fail to obtain men of substantive learning and genuine talent to fulfill the Dynasty's intention of seeking the worthy. When the examination concluded, we obtained one hundred and thirty-five candidates whose essays met the standard. Ah, how flourishing indeed! title: 成化十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
聖子神孫億萬載無疆之業必立
法制垂成憲以開億萬載太
平之治惟賢為治本乃設進
士科取之經術盖非科目不
足以得才而經術之外皆非
學也故前代取士之別塗詞
賦之末習一切罷黜
===
明詔有曰務在經明行修博古
通今文質得中名實相稱大哉
責實求賢之意乎其法周其
制一其為治道計宏且遠矣
列聖相承祗若
祖訓俊乂登庸用熙庶績駸駸乎
虞周之盛非漢唐宋可儗也

足以得才而經術之外皆非

===
明詔有曰務在經明行修博古
通今文質得中名實相稱大哉
責實求賢之意乎其法周其
制一其為治道計宏且遠矣
列聖相承祗若
祖訓俊乂登庸用熈庶績駸駸乎
虞周之盛非漢唐宋可儗也
punctuated: 聖子神孫億萬載無疆之業，必立法制、垂成憲，以開億萬載太平之治。惟賢為治本，乃設進士科，取之經術。盖非科目不足以得才，而經術之外皆非學也。故前代取士之別塗、詞賦之末習，一切罷黜。明詔有曰：「務在經明行修，博古通今，文質得中，名實相稱。」大哉，責實求賢之意乎！其法周，其制一，其為治道計宏且遠矣。列聖相承，祗若祖訓，俊乂登庸，用熙庶績，駸駸乎虞、周之盛，非漢、唐、宋可儗也。
translation_en: …a boundless patrimony for tens of thousands of years to His sagely sons and divine grandsons, He necessarily established laws and institutions and handed down completed statutes to inaugurate a reign of great peace for tens of thousands of years. Considering that worthy men are the foundation of governance, He instituted the metropolitan graduate (jinshi) examination category, selecting them through mastery of the Classics. For indeed, without examination categories it is insufficient to obtain talent, and anything outside mastery of the Classics is not true learning. Therefore, the alternative paths for selecting scholars and the trivial practices of poetic composition of former dynasties were altogether abolished and rejected. His brilliant proclamation states: "The essential thing is that they be versed in the Classics and cultivated in conduct, broadly learned in antiquity and conversant with the present, achieving a balance between literary grace and substantial content, with reputation and reality corresponding to one another." Great indeed is this intention of demanding substance and seeking out the worthy! Its methods are comprehensive, its system is unified, and its planning for the Way of governance is vast and far-reaching. Successive sagely emperors have inherited it one after another, reverently complying with the Ancestral Instructions; men of eminent talent have been elevated and employed, thereby brightening all achievements—rapidly approaching the flourishing ages of Yu and Zhou, which Han, Tang, and Song cannot match.

title: 成化十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
皇上以
聖繼
聖心其心法其法崇奬儒術鼓舞
而造就之者益至于時海內
之士爭自磨濯而文風丕振
倍蓰于昔盖上有好者下必
爭先趨之有不期而然也况
===
治化百年之久
聖德感人之易而太學賢關畿甸
首善之地得之尤先者乎宜
其得士獨最諸藩皆英英乎
氣之充也彬彬乎才之碩也
卓卓乎論議之確而非章句
口耳之空言也噫盛矣哉雖

卓卓乎論議之確而非章句
口耳之空言也噫盛矣哉雖
punctuated: 皇上以聖繼聖，心其心，法其法，崇奬儒術，鼓舞而造就之者益至。于時海內之士爭自磨濯，而文風丕振，倍蓰于昔。盖上有好者，下必爭先趨之，有不期而然也。况治化百年之久，聖德感人之易，而太學賢關、畿甸首善之地，得之尤先者乎！宜其得士獨最諸藩，皆英英乎氣之充也，彬彬乎才之碩也，卓卓乎論議之確，而非章句口耳之空言也。噫，盛矣哉！雖
translation_en: His Majesty, as a sage succeeding sages, makes their minds his mind and their laws his laws, exalting and encouraging Confucian learning, inspiring and cultivating scholars with ever greater thoroughness. At this time, scholars within the seas vie to polish and purify themselves, and the literary ethos flourishes grandly, manifold what it was in the past. For when the ruler above holds a preference, those below will inevitably vie to be first to pursue it; this happens without being demanded. How much more so when transformative governance has endured for a hundred years, when sage virtue moves people with ease, and when the National University—the gateway of the worthy—and the metropolitan region—the place of foremost goodness—are the very first to receive its influence! It is fitting indeed that its success in obtaining scholars surpasses all the provinces: all are brilliant in the fullness of their vital spirit, refined in the greatness of their talent, and outstanding in the soundness of their deliberations, rather than engaging in the empty words of mere chapter-and-verse and rote learning. Ah, how flourishing it is! Even…

title: 成化十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
然所貴乎學者明體而適諸
用也士窮年佔畢夫豈利祿
圖固將以行之也
國家求賢抑豈為觀美哉無非
欲得天下才為天下用焉耳
諸士子所學何如所負何如
而策名是錄其榮且幸又何
===
如能不思所以自振也哉行
與天下士角進而對揚
清問以有官序尚展所抱蘊見
諸事功之實著忠義於
朝廷霈膏澤於黎庶益隆我
國家億萬載太平之治庶幾上
不負

punctuated: 然所貴乎學者，明體而適諸用也。士窮年佔畢，夫豈利祿圖？固將以行之也。國家求賢，抑豈為觀美哉？無非欲得天下才為天下用焉耳。諸士子所學何如？所負何如？而策名是錄，其榮且幸又何如？能不思所以自振也哉！行與天下士角進，而對揚清問，以有官序。尚展所抱蘊，見諸事功之實，著忠義於朝廷，霈膏澤於黎庶，益隆我國家億萬載太平之治，庶幾上不負
translation_en: …that being so, what is valued in learning is illuminating the fundamental substance and applying it in practice. When scholars spend their years poring over texts, how could it merely be a scheme for profit and emolument? Surely it is so that they may put their learning into practice. And when the dynasty seeks worthies, how could it merely be for fine spectacle? It is simply a desire to obtain the talents of the realm for the use of the realm. What is the nature of what you gentlemen have studied? What is the nature of the aspirations you bear? And now that your names are inscribed in this record, how great are your honor and good fortune? How could you not reflect on how to rouse yourselves to action! Soon you will advance to compete alongside the scholars of the entire realm, respond to the Emperor's luminous inquiries, and thereby attain official rank. May you unfold the learning and principles you cherish within, manifest them in the reality of practical achievements, display loyalty and righteousness at court, shower enriching blessings upon the common people, and further exalt our dynasty's rule of great peace for ten thousand myriad years—so that above, you may perchance not fail…

title: 成化十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
天子下不負所學而環等之責亦
少塞萬一其或選耎而無為
跅弛而無不為欺世盜名舉
平生而棄之皆非所謂才也
皆非所謂學也嗚呼是豈直
諸士子之羞
翰林院修撰鄭環謹序

跅弛而無不為欺世盜名舉

皆非所謂學也嗚呼是豈直
諸士子之羞

punctuated:
天子，下不負所學，而環等之責亦少塞萬一。其或選耎而無為，跅弛而無不為，欺世盜名，舉平生而棄之，皆非所謂才也，皆非所謂學也。嗚呼！是豈直諸士子之羞？
翰林院修撰鄭環謹序。
translation_en:
…the Son of Heaven above, nor betray what they have learned below, and the responsibility of myself, [Zheng] Huan, and my colleagues will also be fulfilled to some small degree. Should there be those who are timid and accomplish nothing, or who are unrestrained and stop at nothing—deceiving the world to steal a reputation and casting aside everything they have stood for throughout their lives—none of this is what is meant by talent, and none of this is what is meant by learning. Alas! Would this be a disgrace merely to the scholars themselves?

Respectfully prefaced by Zheng Huan 鄭環, Senior Compiler of the Hanlin Academy (Hanlinyuan xiuzhuan).
